title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄序
甲子歲海宴河淸人文化洽
我
皇上御極之二十三年也是秋適
當掄秀於鄉臣以關西庸儒
辦事禮曹屬閩兩粤之役臣
部疏名答請
===
上命臣茂泰偕王事臣銓往典蜀
試臣職固然臣心實懼西蜀
僻處天末兵燹之後絃誦幾
何且辛酉科鄉試癸亥旣補
行矣才猶木也山雖美工師
數往杞梓椅桐不虞其竭乎
而非也才猶水也不汲則滯
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄序

甲子歲，海宴河淸，人文化洽，我皇上御極之二十三年也。是秋適當掄秀於鄉，臣以關西庸儒，辦事禮曹。屬閩、兩粤之役，臣部疏名答請，上命臣茂泰偕王事臣銓往典蜀試。臣職固然，臣心實懼。西蜀僻處天末，兵燹之後，絃誦幾何？且辛酉科鄉試，癸亥旣補行矣。才猶木也，山雖美，工師數往，杞、梓、椅、桐，不虞其竭乎？而非也。才猶水也，不汲則滯，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the jiazi year (1684), the seas were calm and the Yellow River ran clear, and cultural refinement spread harmoniously everywhere; it was the twenty-third year of Our August Emperor's reign. This autumn was the appointed time for selecting outstanding talents in the provinces. Your servant, an ordinary Confucian scholar from Guanxi, was handling affairs in the Ministry of Rites. On the occasion of the examination missions to Fujian and the two Guang provinces [?], my ministry submitted a memorial listing names to request imperial appointment [?]. The Emperor commanded your servant Maotai, together with Secretary [主事, written 王事] your servant Quan, to go and preside over the examination in Shu (Sichuan). Although this is naturally my official duty, in my heart I was truly apprehensive. Western Shu lies in a remote corner at the ends of the earth; after the devastations of war, how many are left to chant the classics to the accompaniment of strings? Moreover, the Provincial Examination of the xinyou cycle (1681) had already been held as a make-up examination in the guihai year (1683). Talent is like timber: even if a mountain is fine, if the master carpenter goes there repeatedly, is there not reason to fear that the willow, catalpa, yi, and paulownia trees will be exhausted? Yet this is not so. Talent is like water: if it is not drawn, it stagnates;…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
汲則愈新蜀俗尚儒雅況遇
右文之
聖主士無不爭自淬厲以期弋獲
是行也固非無才之慮有才
而未能拔十得五不克勝任
之懼也臣出
京師古燕地星馳就道歷晉歷
秦始抵蜀省途次中三易晦
朔而臣不覺遠
===
天威咫尺赫赫若前日也出井陘
踰霍嶺渡大河陟雲棧巴閬
之間牟勝鳥道幾不可名狀
而臣不覺險
皇路清平利有攸往也旣至監臨
punctuated: 汲則愈新。蜀俗尚儒雅，況遇右文之聖主，士無不爭自淬厲，以期弋獲。是行也，固非無才之慮，有才而未能拔十得五、不克勝任之懼也。臣出京師古燕地，星馳就道，歷晉歷秦，始抵蜀省。途次中三易晦朔，而臣不覺遠，天威咫尺，赫赫若前日也；出井陘，踰霍嶺，渡大河，陟雲棧，巴閬之間，牟勝鳥道，幾不可名狀，而臣不覺險，皇路清平，利有攸往也。旣至，監臨…
translation_en:
…when drawn, it becomes ever fresher. The customs of Shu esteem Confucian elegance; how much more so upon encountering a Sage Sovereign who honors civil culture, so that scholars all vie to temper and exert themselves in hopes of achieving success. On this journey, my concern is certainly not a lack of talent, but rather the fear that where talent exists, I may fail to select five out of ten and prove unequal to my charge.

Your servant departed from the Capital, the ancient land of Yan, hastening along the road by starlight, passing through Jin [Shanxi] and Qin [Shaanxi] before finally reaching the provincial capital of Shu [Sichuan]. Along the way, the moon waned and waxed three times, yet Your servant did not feel the distance to be far, for the Imperial Majesty remained within a foot's breadth, awe-inspiring as if it were only the day before. Emerging from the Jingxing Pass, crossing the Huo Mountains, fording the Yellow River, and ascending the Cloud Plank Roads, amid Ba and Lang the rugged terrain [?] and bird-paths were almost beyond description, yet Your servant did not feel the peril, for the Imperial highway is clear and peaceful, making it favorable to have somewhere to go. Upon arrival, the Supervising Official…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
則巡撫部院兵部尚書右副
都御史臣世琦防維劫慫霜
霆共凜提調則布政使臣顯
第松威道僉事臣隲經畫周
詳庶務咸秩監試則按察使
臣業與川東道僉事臣焜㦸
持憲章內外交飭同考官聘
===
之隣封者經義有聲則學正
臣璇教諭臣國麟臣振臣桂
臣光台遴之本省者循良著
譽則知縣臣震元臣錫祚臣
光華臣元科臣星著臣等相
與誓神受事採策定題進提
學僉事臣馮雲驤所取士一
punctuated: 則巡撫部院、兵部尚書、右副都御史臣世琦，防維劫慫，霜霆共凜；提調則布政使臣顯第、松威道僉事臣隲，經畫周詳，庶務咸秩；監試則按察使臣業與、川東道僉事臣焜，㦸持憲章，內外交飭。同考官聘之隣封者，經義有聲，則學正臣璇，教諭臣國麟、臣振、臣桂、臣光台；遴之本省者，循良著譽，則知縣臣震元、臣錫祚、臣光華、臣元科、臣星著。臣等相與誓神受事，採策定題，進提學僉事臣馮雲驤所取士一
translation_en: … the Supervising Official was Grand Coordinator, Minister of War, and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, His Majesty's servant [Han] Shiqi 世琦, whose precautions and strictures [防維劫慫; 劫慫 is a transcription error for 劼毖, "earnest and cautious" (?)] inspired universal awe like frost and thunder; the Proctors were Administration Commissioner, His Majesty's servant [Lang] Xiandi 顯第, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Song-Wei Circuit, His Majesty's servant [Wang] Zhi 隲, whose planning was thorough and detailed so that all affairs were in good order; the Monitoring Officials were Surveillance Commissioner, His Majesty's servant [Zhou] Yeyu 業與, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Eastern Sichuan Circuit, His Majesty's servant [Zhang] Kun 焜, who sternly upheld [㦸持; 㦸 is a transcription error for 職 or 執 (?)] the statutory regulations, maintaining discipline both inside and outside the compound. Among the Associate Examiners, those invited from neighboring provinces who were renowned for their mastery of classical exegesis were Department Director of Schools, His Majesty's servant Xuan 璇, and District Directors of Schools, His Majesty's servants Guolin 國麟, Zhen 振, Gui 桂, and Guangtai 光台; those selected from within this province who had earned reputations as upright and capable administrators were District Magistrates, His Majesty's servants Zhenyuan 震元, Xizuo 錫祚, Guanghua 光華, Yuanke 元科, and Xingzhu 星著. Your servants together swore an oath before the spirits and took up our duties, drew lots to determine the examination topics, and admitted the one [thousand one hundred and more] scholars selected by Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education, His Majesty's servant Feng Yunxiang 馮雲驤…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
千一百有奇局闈三試之正
色凝神嚴覈詳閱十餘日矢
公矢慎依舊額所定合康熈
二十年
恩詔所增拔其尤者四十九人副
於榜者八人錄其文二十篇
以
===
獻臣例得颺言簡端臣惟取士
之法前莫善於鄉舉里選而
後莫善於制科則時爲之也
其人才之盛在五帝則推唐
虞曰敷奏以言明試以功而
十六才子之舉於家者爲天
下所共稱在三代則美有周
punctuated:
千一百有奇，局闈三試之。正色凝神，嚴覈詳閱十餘日，矢公矢慎，依舊額所定，合康熈二十年恩詔所增，拔其尤者四十九人，副於榜者八人，錄其文二十篇以獻。臣例得颺言簡端。
臣惟取士之法，前莫善於鄉舉里選，而後莫善於制科，則時爲之也。其人才之盛，在五帝則推唐虞，曰「敷奏以言，明試以功」，而十六才子之舉於家者，爲天下所共稱；在三代則美有周，
translation_en:
… thousand one hundred and more, and locked the examination compound to test them in three sessions. With solemn countenance and concentrated spirit, we strictly verified and carefully read the papers for more than ten days, vowing to be impartial and cautious. In accordance with the established old quota, combined with the increase granted by the gracious edict of the twentieth year of the Kangxi reign (1681), we selected the forty-nine most outstanding candidates, along with eight placed on the supplementary list (fubang), and recorded twenty of their essays to present to the throne. By precedent, your servant is permitted to offer words at the beginning of the volume.
Your servant reflects that among the methods of selecting scholars, in earlier times none was better than recommendation by district and village, while in later times none has been better than the regular civil service examinations; this is brought about by the times. As for the flourishing of men of talent, among the Five Emperors one praises Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], of which it is said, "They set forth reports in words, and are clearly tested by merits," and the "sixteen talented sons" (shiliu caizi) raised up from their families were praised together by all under Heaven. Among the Three Dynasties, one admires the house of Zhou, …

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
曰建官惟賢位事惟能而賢
能之書大司徒賓興於鄉而
後獻之王此選舉所由得也
漢唐以來賢良方正而外又
有有道直言九品中正對策
詩賦等條世風不古取士之
法亦屢易而不能經久宋始
===
定爲八股之格終明之世用
以取士我
朝損益前代制科一準有明而又
詳定條例慎選真才四十年
來制科得人之盛較古之鄉
舉里選何多讓焉然而臣猶
有進焉者
punctuated: 曰：「建官惟賢，位事惟能。」而賢能之書，大司徒賓興於鄉，而後獻之王，此選舉所由得也。漢、唐以來，賢良方正而外，又有有道、直言、九品中正、對策、詩賦等條。世風不古，取士之法亦屢易而不能經久。宋始定爲八股之格，終明之世用以取士。我朝損益前代，制科一準有明，而又詳定條例，慎選真才。四十年來，制科得人之盛，較古之鄉舉里選，何多讓焉？然而臣猶有進焉者，
translation_en: … saying: "Establish in office only the worthy; place in charge of affairs only the capable." As for the registers of the worthy and the capable, the Grand Minister of Instruction (da situ 大司徒) treated them as honored guests and raised them up from the districts, and only afterward presented them to the King; this is whereby the selection and recommendation of talent succeeded. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, besides the categories of the "Worthy and Good, Square and Upright" (xianliang fangzheng 賢良方正), there were also such categories as "Possessing the Way" (youdao 有道), "Outspoken Admonition" (zhiyan 直言), the Nine-Rank Impartial Judges (jiupin zhongzheng 九品中正), policy responses (duice 對策), and poetry and rhapsodies (shifu 詩賦). As the customs of the age fell short of antiquity, the methods for selecting scholars also changed repeatedly and could not endure for long. Only in the Song was the eight-legged essay (bagu 八股) format established, and throughout the Ming era it was used to select scholars. Our Dynasty has adapted the institutions of previous eras by trimming and augmenting them; the regular civil service examinations (zhike 制科) entirely follow the standards of the Ming, while also establishing detailed regulations to carefully select genuine talent. Over the past forty years, how does the flourishing abundance of talent obtained through the regular civil service examinations yield anything to the ancient system of district recommendation and village selection? Yet your servant still has something further to offer: …

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
國家之取人責實効也公孤卿
尹皆多士可躋之名位惠疇
亮釆皆多士可爲之事業而
欲以三朝之文藝定其終身
則臣不敢知蜀之先若張綱
何煥杜莘老等直節著矣而
不必盡優於文詩如李白法
===
言如楊雄賦如司馬相如文
詞炳矣而行事不無可議惟
陳堯叟陳堯咨文擢第一蘇
軾蘇轍文號大家而居官之
治行亦皆不媿科名斯又不
世出之儒而欲一一望之後
人則臣不敢知雖然經術即
punctuated: 國家之取人，責實効也。公孤卿尹，皆多士可躋之名位；惠疇亮釆，皆多士可爲之事業。而欲以三朝之文藝，定其終身，則臣不敢知。蜀之先，若張綱、何煥、杜莘老等，直節著矣，而不必盡優於文；詩如李白、《法言》如楊雄、賦如司馬相如，文詞炳矣，而行事不無可議。惟陳堯叟、陳堯咨文擢第一，蘇軾、蘇轍文號大家，而居官之治行亦皆不媿科名，斯又不世出之儒。而欲一一望之後人，則臣不敢知。雖然，經術即
translation_en: The State selects men by demanding practical results. The Three Dukes, Three Solitaries, Nine Ministers, and Directors are all illustrious positions to which the many scholars may ascend; harmonizing the categories of governance and brightening the affairs of state are all enterprises that the many scholars may accomplish. Yet if one wished to determine their entire lives on the basis of the literary compositions of three mornings, that your servant would not dare claim to know. Among the worthies of Shu in former times, men such as Zhang Gang 張綱, He Huan 何煥, and Du Xinlao 杜莘老 were renowned for their upright integrity, yet they did not necessarily all excel in literature; whereas with poetry like that of Li Bai 李白, Model Sayings (Fayan 法言) like that of Yang Xiong 楊雄, and rhapsodies (fu 賦) like those of Sima Xiangru 司馬相如, their literary expressions were resplendent indeed, yet their conduct was not beyond criticism. Only Chen Yaosou 陳堯叟 and Chen Yaozi 陳堯咨, who were selected first in the literary examinations, and Su Shi 蘇軾 and Su Zhe 蘇轍, who were acclaimed as great masters of prose, also proved in their administrative conduct while in office to be entirely worthy of their examination honors—yet these were Confucian scholars of a kind that does not appear in every generation. To expect all of this one by one from men of later times is something your servant would not dare claim to know. Even so, classical scholarship is precisely…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
所以經世殆未可輕量天下
士也即多士異日之治行臣
不可知而經術之夾見之於
尺牘行墨中者已無不可知
臣知其所可知而不可知者
是在多士自勉之而臣尤欲
其共勉之則進而易之以言
===
逆者隣滇逞逆禍連全蜀
皇上神武蕩平出湯火而登衽席
平賦徭補鄉試今秋相繼賓
興教養兼至知是者宜何以
報爾蜀峩眉岷江形勝甲於
天下多士鍾川嶽之秀既聽
鹿鳴而登賢書矣再進而捷
punctuated: 所以經世，殆未可輕量天下士也。即多士異日之治行，臣不可知，而經術之夾見之於尺牘行墨中者，已無不可知。臣知其所可知，而不可知者，是在多士自勉之。而臣尤欲其共勉之，則進而易之以言：逆者隣滇逞逆，禍連全蜀。皇上神武蕩平，出湯火而登衽席，平賦徭，補鄉試。今秋相繼賓興，教養兼至。知是者，宜何以報？爾蜀峩眉、岷江，形勝甲於天下。多士鍾川嶽之秀，既聽鹿鳴而登賢書矣，再進而捷
translation_en:
…that by which one orders the world; thus one surely ought not take lightly the scholars of the realm. Even though I cannot know the administrative achievements of you scholars in future days, the classical learning that is seen interspersed [夾; 愀/概?] within the pages and lines of your scripts is already something that can be fully known. I know what can be known, while as for what cannot yet be known, it rests with you scholars to strive for it yourselves. Yet I especially wish for you all to strive together, and so I bring you forward and exhort [易, for 勗?] you with these words:

Recently [逆者, for 曩者], neighboring Yunnan unleashed rebellion, and the calamity spread across all of Sichuan. His Majesty, through his divine martial prowess, swept away and pacified the rebels, rescuing the people from boiling water and fire and placing them upon peaceful sleeping mats. He equalized taxes and corvée labor and held a make-up Provincial Examination; this autumn, in succession, the推薦 of local worthies (binxing) is again taking place, bringing both education and nourishment to perfection. For those who understand this, how ought you to repay such grace?

In your Sichuan, Mount Emei and the Min River rank first in the realm in strategic beauty. You scholars, imbued with the finest essence of these rivers and peaks, have now heard the "Criing of the Deer" (Luming) ode and had your names entered in the register of worthies. Advancing once more to triumph…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
南宮對
丹陛當
欽賜進士及第出身有差近又疏
通銓選庶常讀書中秘郎出
宰百里者亦得指日結綬治
成遷擢惠疇亮采公孤卿尹
豈異人任與惟尊聞行知本
===
經術以經世勿自負其先資
勿狹小其懷來勿使陳堯叟
蘇軾兄弟之文章治行獨高
千古以爲制科光臣庶幾借
以拜手稽首少釋隕越之懼
也已多士勉乎哉維時有事
茲土者總督四川陝西文武
punctuated:
南宮，對丹陛，當欽賜進士及第、出身有差。近又疏通銓選，庶常讀書中秘，郎出宰百里者，亦得指日結綬，治成遷擢。惠疇亮采，公孤卿尹，豈異人任與？惟尊聞行知，本經術以經世，勿自負其先資，勿狹小其懷來，勿使陳堯叟、蘇軾兄弟之文章治行獨高千古，以爲制科光，臣庶幾借以拜手稽首，少釋隕越之懼也已。多士勉乎哉！
維時有事茲土者：總督四川陝西文武
translation_en:
… in the Southern Palace [Metropolitan Examination] and reply before the Vermilion Steps [in the Palace Examination], you shall be imperially granted the degrees of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi) or metropolitan graduate (jinshi chushen) according to rank. Recently, the selection and appointment process has also been cleared of bottlenecks: Hanlin Bachelors (shuchang) study in the Inner Secretariat, and even those who go out directly to govern a county of a hundred li can expect to tie on their official ribbon in no time, and upon achieving good governance, be promoted. To kindly govern the populace and brightly assist in state affairs, serving as Dukes, Three Solitaries, Ministers, or Directors—is that the responsibility of anyone other than yourselves? Only honor what you have heard and practice what you know; ground yourselves in classical scholarship in order to order the world; do not betray your initial qualifications [by which you pledged yourself to service]; do not narrow the scope of your aspirations; and do not let the literary writings and administrative achievements of the brothers of Chen Yaosou 陳堯叟 and Su Shi 蘇軾 stand alone in towering above all antiquity, so that you may bring glory to the civil service examinations. Your servant may perhaps avail himself of this to bow with hands folded to the ground and slightly relieve his fear of failing in his duties. May you gentlemen strive onward!

At this time, those holding office in this region are: Supreme Commander (zongdu) of Civil and Military…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
事務兼理糧餉兵部尚書兼
都察院右都御史臣希福提
督四川等處地方軍務節制
全省鎮將提調漢土官兵總
兵官都督同知加二級臣何
傅鎮守四川松潘等處地方
總兵官都督同知臣高鼎鎮
===
守四川重慶等處地方總兵
官左都督世襲拖沙喇哈番
仍記餘功三次臣王度冲鎮
守四川川北等處地方總兵
官左都督仍記功五次加二

text:
第壹場
四書
言寡尤行寡悔祿在其中矣
體羣臣則士之報禮重
民日遷善而不知爲之者
易
君子體仁足以長人
益動而巽日進无疆
夫易廣矣大矣
===
聚而上者謂之升
書
彰厥有常吉哉
念終始典于學
是訓是行以近天子之光
思其艱以圖其易民乃寧
詩
孑孑干旌在浚之城
攸介攸止烝我髦士
punctuated:
第壹場

四書：
「言寡尤，行寡悔，祿在其中矣。」
「體羣臣，則士之報禮重。」
「民日遷善，而不知爲之者。」

易：
「君子體仁，足以長人。」
「益，動而巽，日進无疆。」
「夫易，廣矣，大矣。」
「聚而上者，謂之升。」

書：
「彰厥有常，吉哉！」
「念終始典于學。」
「是訓是行，以近天子之光。」
「思其艱以圖其易，民乃寧。」

詩：
「孑孑干旌，在浚之城。」
「攸介攸止，烝我髦士。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books:
"When one's words give few occasions for blame, and one's conduct gives few occasions for regret, emolument is contained therein."
"By showing sympathetic consideration to the body of officials, the gentlemen will repay courtesies heavily."
"The people move daily toward goodness without knowing who brings it about."

Classic of Changes (Yi):
"The noble man embodies benevolence and is thus sufficient to be a leader of men."
"Increase (Yi): movement and penetration; advancing daily without limit."
"Now the Changes—how vast they are, how great they are!"
"Gathering together and ascending is called Pushing Upward (Sheng)."

Classic of Documents (Shu):
"Display constancy in your virtue—how auspicious!"
"Fix your thoughts from beginning to end constantly on learning."
"Take this as your instruction, take this as your practice, and so draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven."
"Think on the difficulties in order to plan for what is easy, and the people will then have peace."

Classic of Odes (Shi):
"Conspicuous rise the ox-tail and falcon-feather banners, at the suburban wall of Xun."
"In a spacious place I halt, to call together and encourage myeminent young men."

translation_en:
"Never idle morning or night, in order to serve the One Man."
"Daily pacifying the four quarters."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"Autumn, the seventh month" [6th year of Duke Yin]; "The Heavenly King sent Jiafu to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [8th year of Duke Huan].
"The feudal lords thereupon relieved Xu" [6th year of Duke Xi]; "The feudal lords thereupon besieged Xu" [28th year of Duke Xi].
"The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng" [1st year of Duke Xuan].
"The people of Qi returned Huan and Chan" [8th year of Duke Ai].

Record of Rites (Liji):
"Exalting the worthy in order to revere virtue."
"Practicing the three pieces of the Lesser Odes is the beginning of preparing them for office."
"When the patterns of music are the same, superiors and inferiors are in harmony."
"When the gentleman is grave and reverent, he becomes stronger day by day."

Second Session
Discourse (Lun):
"Lead them first with reverence and deference, and the people will not contend."

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
必有一代致治之道此唐虞三代所以
化臻隆理長治久安而爲後世所不能
及也漢唐宋以來亦有願治之主而其
治效遠不逮古何歟或治法之徒立而
所爲致治之道未嘗謹始圖終基命宥
密求詳於其間歟我
皇上承
昊天之眷命紹
祖宗之光烈
===
聖學日新
神謀廣運文德武功駕軼前代山陬海澨悉入
版圖紀綱燦著聲教四訖治化之隆薄
海内外一道同風矣而猶勵精圖治孜
孜不遑日厪念乎民生之安養政治之
修舉
睿慮周詳罔無俟凡庸之過計然幸際承平欣
逢
盛治思所以仰裨萬一其道將何在歟夫從
punctuated: 必有一代致治之道，此唐虞三代所以化臻隆理、長治久安，而爲後世所不能及也。漢唐宋以來，亦有願治之主，而其治效遠不逮古，何歟？或治法之徒立，而所爲致治之道未嘗謹始圖終、基命宥密，求詳於其間歟？我皇上承昊天之眷命，紹祖宗之光烈，聖學日新，神謀廣運，文德武功駕軼前代，山陬海澨悉入版圖，紀綱燦著，聲教四訖，治化之隆，薄海内外一道同風矣。而猶勵精圖治，孜孜不遑，日厪念乎民生之安養、政治之修舉。睿慮周詳，罔無俟凡庸之過計，然幸際承平，欣逢盛治，思所以仰裨萬一，其道將何在歟？夫從
translation_en:
… there has necessarily been a Way of bringing about order for that dynasty. This is why in the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, transformative rule reached the height of good governance, achieving lasting order and enduring peace that later ages have been unable to match. Since the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, there have also been rulers who desired good governance, yet the results of their rule fell far short of antiquity—why is this? Could it be that methods of governance were merely established in name, while as for the Way of bringing about order, they never attended carefully to the beginning and planned for the end, or grounded their mandate in quiet, unceasing devotion, seeking thoroughness therein?

Our August Emperor has received the favored Mandate of Vast Heaven and inherited the glorious achievements of His Ancestors. His sage learning is daily renewed and His divine counsels operate far and wide; His civil virtue and military achievements surpass those of former dynasties. Every mountain corner and seashore has been brought into the register of the realm; state discipline shines forth brilliantly, and imperial prestige and teachings reach in all four directions. In the flourishing of His governance and transformation, all within and beyond the seas follow the same Way and share the same customs. Yet He still exerts Himself tirelessly to seek good governance, diligently allowing Himself no leisure, and daily cherishes anxious concern for the peaceful livelihood of the people and the promotion and reform of administration. His imperial deliberations are comprehensive and thorough, certainly having no need for the excessive calculations of ordinary men; yet, fortunate to live in an era of peace and rejoicing to encounter this flourishing reign, if we reflect on how to offer even a ten-thousandth part of assistance to His Majesty, wherein shall that Way lie? Now, ever…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
來國家有已安已治之日而帝王之爲
治者不存已安已治之心是以史載虞
廷之治四方風動而君臣相誥誡者一
則曰儆戒無虞一則曰勑天之命惟時
惟幾周公告成王曰君子所其無逸豈
非古聖之心法爲道法所從出而一代
之治法本諸道法而盡善歟則當海宇
昇平之日爲
國家萬年有道之長保世滋大以上媲隆古
其道固有在也爾多士留心經濟盍昌
言之將藉手以爲
當宁獻
===
問治天下者審所尚所尚既定而風俗成
人心亦因之正則移風易俗使天下回
心而嚮道不綦重歟夫風俗之美始於
儉而成於厚其弊也始於奢而成於僭
乃人性之厭樸而喜華世情之好奢而
惡嗇也如水之趨下易就難返若無所
punctuated:
來國家有已安已治之日，而帝王之爲治者，不存已安已治之心。是以史載虞廷之治，四方風動，而君臣相誥誡者，一則曰：「儆戒無虞。」一則曰：「勑天之命，惟時惟幾。」周公告成王曰：「君子所其無逸。」豈非古聖之心法爲道法所從出，而一代之治法本諸道法而盡善歟？則當海宇昇平之日，爲國家萬年有道之長，保世滋大，以上媲隆古，其道固有在也。爾多士留心經濟，盍昌言之，將藉手以爲當宁獻。
問：治天下者審所尚，所尚既定而風俗成，人心亦因之正。則移風易俗，使天下回心而嚮道，不綦重歟？夫風俗之美，始於儉而成於厚；其弊也，始於奢而成於僭。乃人性之厭樸而喜華，世情之好奢而惡嗇也，如水之趨下，易就難返。若無所
translation_en:
… ever since antiquity, a state may experience days when security and order have already been achieved, yet emperors and kings who govern do not harbor a mindset that security and order have already been achieved. Therefore, history records that in the governance of the court of Yu, the four quarters were moved as if by the wind; yet when ruler and ministers admonished one another, on the one hand they said, "Be cautious and vigilant when there is no cause for anxiety," and on the other hand they said, "Revere the mandate of Heaven, at every moment and in the slightest beginnings." The Duke of Zhou (Zhougong) told King Cheng (Chengwang), "The noble man makes 'taking no ease' his dwelling place." Is it not the case that the mental discipline of the ancient sages is the source from which the principles of the Way emerge, and that the methods of governance of an era attain perfection by being rooted in those principles of the Way? Then, in this day of peace throughout the realm, to ensure ten thousand years of righteous longevity for the State, preserving the world and making it ever greater so as to rival the glorious antiquity above—there is surely a proper way for this. You many scholars have paid close attention to statecraft; why not speak forthrightly of it, so that we may use your words as an offering to the Throne?

Question: Those who govern All-under-Heaven carefully examine what is esteemed. Once what is esteemed is settled, customs and mores are formed, and human minds are rectified accordingly. Then is not transforming customs and changing mores, so as to cause All-under-Heaven to turn their hearts and incline toward the Way, of the utmost importance? Now, the excellence of customs begins in frugality and is completed in generosity; their corruption begins in extravagance and culminates in僭 (usurpation of status). Yet human nature's distaste for simplicity and fondness for splendor, and worldly sentiment's love of extravagance and dislike of thrift, are like water flowing downward—easy to follow and hard to reverse. If there is no means by which to …

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
以轉移化導之豈能使奢靡之不作而
風尚之咸歸於淳厚乎我
國家統一區宇釐定典章文不過奢質不近
陋
皇上躬行節儉端軌率物以爲天下先宜化行
俗美比屋可封而猶有浮靡是尚僭侈
成習不盡返淳還樸如古郅隆之盛者
豈民性之不古若歟抑所以轉移化導
者有司之奉行未力歟孝弟力田之科
===
可復設乎陳詩納價之制可復舉乎節
性防淫之典可倣古而行之乎大易履
卦象曰君子以辯上下定民志記曰禮
至則不爭然則禮制行而民志以定咸
凜然於天秩天敘之大經而不敢有僭
紊以日流於奢靡者轉移化導之機豈
無其要歟多士悉抒所見以對
問王者任德不任刑刑者聖王不得已而
用之者也舜命皋陶明刑弼教曰刑期
punctuated:
以轉移化導之，豈能使奢靡之不作，而風尚之咸歸於淳厚乎？我國家統一區宇，釐定典章，文不過奢，質不近陋。皇上躬行節儉，端軌率物，以爲天下先，宜化行俗美，比屋可封；而猶有浮靡是尚、僭侈成習，不盡返淳還樸，如古郅隆之盛者，豈民性之不古若歟？抑所以轉移化導者，有司之奉行未力歟？孝弟力田之科可復設乎？陳詩納價之制可復舉乎？節性防淫之典可倣古而行之乎？《大易》〈履〉卦《象》曰：「君子以辯上下，定民志。」《記》曰：「禮至則不爭。」然則禮制行而民志以定，咸凜然於天秩天敘之大經，而不敢有僭紊以日流於奢靡者，轉移化導之機，豈無其要歟？多士悉抒所見以對。

問：王者任德不任刑，刑者，聖王不得已而用之者也。舜命皋陶明刑弼教，曰：「刑期
translation_en:
…by which to transform and guide them, how can one prevent extravagance from arising and bring customs wholly back to simplicity and generosity? Our dynasty has unified the realm and established statutes and regulations, wherein refinement does not exceed into extravagance and substance does not border on crudeness. The Emperor personally practices frugality, setting an upright standard to lead all things and placing himself at the forefront of the empire. Moral transformation should prevail and customs should be admirable, such that every household is worthy of enfeoffment. Yet there are still those who prize superficial extravagance and make a habit of sumptuous usurpation, not entirely returning to simplicity and plainness as in the flourishing ages of antiquity. Is this because the nature of the people is not what it was in ancient times? Or is it that the authorities have not been diligent enough in carrying out the means of transformation and guidance? Can the special categories of filial piety, fraternal submission, and diligent farming be re-established? Can the institution of presenting folk songs and reporting market prices be revived? Can the statutes for moderating human nature and preventing licentiousness be put into practice in imitation of antiquity? In the Great Changes (Yijing), the "Image" commentary on the "Treading" (Lü) hexagram states: "The superior man thereby discriminates between high and low, and settles the aims of the people." The Record of Rites (Liji) states: "When ritual reaches its perfection, there is no contention." If ritual regulations are put into effect so that the aims of the people are settled, and all stand in awe of the great norms of Heaven-ordained ranks and orders without daring to commit presumptuous infractions or slide daily into extravagance, does not the pivotal mechanism of transformation and guidance have its essential point? Let you many scholars fully express your views in reply.

Question: A true king relies on virtue and not on punishments; punishments are what sage kings use only when they have no alternative. Shun commanded Gao Yao to clarify punishments in order to assist moral instruction, saying, "Punishments are intended…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
于無刑以至禹湯之泣罪解網其心一
古帝欽恤之心也周自文武至于成康
深仁厚澤歷數十年刑措不用論者謂
太和在成周宇宙間休哉何風之古歟
三代而下有詔除肉刑史稱其禁網疎
濶幾于刑措者矣有禁笞囚背詔死罪
雖即決仍三覆奏者矣有注意刑辟非
情理深害多得寛貸者矣是皆於明罰
勑法之中寓寛仁惻怛之意可為指陳
之歟我
===
皇上仁慈性成視民如傷
勑刑官問擬不得偏引重條情罪大者必令法
司核擬又嚴立限期俾無寃滯與古所
稱如天好生之仁曠代同符矣而人輕
犯法罹辟者亦復不少何歟夫獄者天
下之大命也死者不可復生絶者不可
復屬民即無良豈甘自罹於法網其元
惡大憝怙終不悛之輩不足恤已外此
punctuated: 于無刑」，以至禹、湯之泣罪解網，其心一古帝欽恤之心也。周自文、武至于成、康，深仁厚澤，歷數十年刑措不用，論者謂太和在成周宇宙間，休哉！何風之古歟！三代而下，有詔除肉刑，史稱其禁網疎濶、幾于刑措者矣；有禁笞囚背、詔死罪雖即決仍三覆奏者矣；有注意刑辟、非情理深害多得寛貸者矣。是皆於明罰勑法之中，寓寛仁惻怛之意，可為指陳之歟？我皇上仁慈性成，視民如傷，勑刑官問擬不得偏引重條，情罪大者必令法司核擬，又嚴立限期，俾無寃滯，與古所稱如天好生之仁，曠代同符矣。而人輕犯法，罹辟者亦復不少，何歟？夫獄者，天下之大命也，死者不可復生，絶者不可復屬。民即無良，豈甘自罹於法網？其元惡大憝、怙終不悛之輩，不足恤已；外此
translation_en: …that there may be no punishments." Down to Yu weeping over criminals and Tang opening the net, their minds were wholly one with the reverent compassion of the ancient emperors. In the Zhou dynasty, from Kings Wen and Wu down to Kings Cheng and Kang, through deep benevolence and generous grace, for several decades punishments were set aside and left unused. Commentators have said that supreme harmony prevailed throughout the universe of the Flourishing Zhou. How splendid! How ancient in spirit were those customs! From the Three Dynasties downward, there was one who issued an edict abolishing corporal mutilation, of whom the histories record that the net of prohibitions was loose and broad, coming close to the setting aside of punishments; there was one who forbade flogging prisoners on the back and decreed that even capital offenses subject to immediate execution must still be reviewed in three memorials; and there was one who paid close attention to penal statutes, granting leniency and pardon in most cases unless the offense was deeply harmful to human feeling and principle. All of these embodied the spirit of寬仁 (lenient benevolence) and compassionate sorrow within the clear application of penalties and the enforcement of law—can you point them out and set them forth? Our August Emperor is benevolent and compassionate by nature, looking upon the people as if they were wounded. He has commanded judicial officials that in trying cases and proposing sentences they must not partially cite severe statutes; where the circumstances and crimes are grave, he invariably orders the Three Judicial Offices to review the proposed sentence, and he has strictly established time limits so that there may be neither wrongful convictions nor delays in custody. This tallies across the ages with what antiquity praised as the heaven-like benevolence that loves life. Yet people lightly violate the law, and those who fall into capital punishment are still not few—why is this? Now, criminal cases are a matter of great life and death for the empire: the dead cannot be brought back to life, and what is severed cannot be reattached. Even if the people are devoid of goodness, how could they willingly cast themselves into the net of the law? As for the arch-criminals and great evildoers who persist in wrong without repentance, they are not worth pitying; beyond these…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
則或陷於無知或誤於比匪亦或懍被
寃誣獄已成而莫爲昭雪者矣今欲法
歸平允俗躋仁壽使天下革心向化媿
美盛古祥刑之風慰
皇上以德化民之至意何道而可多士毋勦毋
枝爲著於篇
問古者戍其地即因其地之宜守其土即
用其土之利屯政尚矣昔人言屯政者
謂屯田一石可當轉輸二十石誠見夫
屯政之利較轉輸爲甚便所當力爲舉
===
行者也我
國家神武戡定兵制視古盡善至養兵之費
取諸正供之額賦士飽馬騰餉不匱而
兵足用數十年於玆矣屯政之利亦有
言及而未之舉行者無亦以井田旣廢
兵農之不復合其來已久欲使披堅執
銳之士令其從事南畝也殆有所難行
乎然亦有當籌屯政於攻取之時
punctuated:
則或陷於無知，或誤於比匪，亦或懍被寃誣，獄已成而莫爲昭雪者矣。今欲法歸平允，俗躋仁壽，使天下革心向化，媿美盛古祥刑之風，慰皇上以德化民之至意，何道而可？多士毋勦毋枝，爲著於篇。
問：古者戍其地即因其地之宜，守其土即用其土之利，屯政尚矣。昔人言屯政者，謂屯田一石，可當轉輸二十石。誠見夫屯政之利，較轉輸爲甚便，所當力爲舉行者也。我國家神武戡定，兵制視古盡善。至養兵之費，取諸正供之額賦，士飽馬騰，餉不匱而兵足用，數十年於玆矣。屯政之利，亦有言及而未之舉行者，無亦以井田旣廢，兵農之不復合其來已久，欲使披堅執銳之士，令其從事南畝也，殆有所難行乎？然亦有當籌屯政於攻取之時，
translation_en:
…then there are those who fall into crime out of ignorance, or are led astray by associating with evildoers, or even tremble under false accusations after their cases have already been finalized with no one to exonerate them. Now, if we wish for the application of the law to return to fairness and equity, and for customs to ascend to benevolence and longevity—causing the whole empire to reform its heart and turn toward moral transformation, rivaling the auspicious penal customs of high antiquity and comforting the Emperor's supreme intention to transform the people through virtue—by what way can this be achieved? Let you many scholars neither plagiarize nor digress, and set forth your views in your essays.
Question: In antiquity, those who garrisoned a region adapted to the suitability of that region, and those who defended a territory utilized the resources of that territory; the administration of military state farms (tunzheng) is of long standing indeed. Those in the past who discussed military state farms said that one picul of grain from a military farm is equivalent to twenty piculs transported from afar. They truly saw that the benefits of military state farms are far more convenient than long-distance transport, and that it is a policy that ought to be vigorously implemented. Our dynasty has pacified the realm through divine martial prowess, and its military system is utterly perfected compared to antiquity. As for the expenses of maintaining the troops, they are drawn from the regular quota of statutory tax revenues; the soldiers are well-fed and the horses spirited, military provisions do not run short, and the troops suffice for use—it has been so for several decades now. The benefits of military state farms have also been spoken of, yet have not been put into practice. Is this not because, since the well-field system was abolished, the separation of soldiers and farmers has existed for a long time, so that if one wished to make men who wear sturdy armor and wield sharp weapons engage in work in the southern fields, it would perhaps be somewhat difficult to carry out? Or is it that when planning military state farms during a time of offensive campaigns…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
方期以克敵致勝復令之旣耕且戰也
自不遑及若海宇蕩平之日寧不可爲
議及乎盡荷戈之衆槩責以耕耘之務
固非所宜若爲之揆度於其間令三分
戍守七分屯種不亦可酌而行之歟從
來不患無治法患無治人漢趙充國留
祐鎭襄陽減戍邏之卒墾田八百餘頃
田金城條便宜十二事卒收其效晉羊
其始至也軍無百日之糧其後乃有十
===
年之積唐郭子儀鎭河中自耕百畝爲
將校先士卒皆不勸而耕遂野無曠土
軍有餘糧皆行之而旣效者古法豈竟
難復歟至如西蜀防鎭之兵星羅棊布
歲需餉額數十萬皆仰給於隣省遠道
崎嶇餽運維艱非經久之長策也誠爲
從長規畫舉行屯政不可以減大農之
派撥免隣省之轉輸歟多士盱衡時事
應有所見試言其可行者
punctuated: 方期以克敵致勝，復令之旣耕且戰也，自不遑及；若海宇蕩平之日，寧不可爲議及乎？盡荷戈之衆，槩責以耕耘之務，固非所宜；若爲之揆度於其間，令三分戍守、七分屯種，不亦可酌而行之歟？從來不患無治法，患無治人。漢趙充國留祐鎭襄陽，減戍邏之卒，墾田八百餘頃；田金城，條便宜十二事，卒收其效。晉羊其始至也，軍無百日之糧；其後乃有十年之積。唐郭子儀鎭河中，自耕百畝，爲將校先，士卒皆不勸而耕，遂野無曠土，軍有餘糧。皆行之而旣效者，古法豈竟難復歟？至如西蜀防鎭之兵，星羅棊布，歲需餉額數十萬，皆仰給於隣省。遠道崎嶇，餽運維艱，非經久之長策也。誠爲從長規畫，舉行屯政，不可以減大農之派撥、免隣省之轉輸歟？多士盱衡時事，應有所見，試言其可行者。
translation_en:
… when one is just looking to vanquish the enemy and secure victory, to further order the troops to both farm and fight simultaneously is naturally something for which there is no leisure. Yet in an era when the realm has been swept clean and pacified, how could it not be brought up for deliberation? To take the entire multitude of spear-bearing soldiers and uniformly charge them with the tasks of plowing and weeding is assuredly inappropriate; yet if one were to weigh and measure the matter between the two, ordering three-tenths to garrison and defend and seven-tenths to farm in colonies, could this not also be deliberated upon and put into practice?

From of old, the worry has never been the lack of methods of governance, but rather the lack of men to govern. In the Han dynasty, Zhao Chongguo趙充國 stayed to farm at Jincheng 金城, setting forth twelve articles of expedient measures, and in the end reaped their results; in the Jin dynasty, Yang Hu 羊祜 garrisoned Xiangyang 襄陽, reducing the soldiers on garrison and patrol duty to open up over eight hundred qing of farmland [? column order transposed in print: "In the Han dynasty, Zhao Chongguo stayed… Hu garrisoned Xiangyang, reducing the soldiers on garrison and patrol duty to open up over eight hundred qing of farmland; …to farm at Jincheng, setting forth twelve articles of expedient measures, and in the end reaped their results. In the Jin dynasty, Yang…"]—when he first arrived, the army did not have provisions for a hundred days, yet afterward it possessed ten years' worth of stores. In the Tang dynasty, Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 garrisoned Hezhong 河中 and personally plowed a hundred mu to set an example for his generals and officers; the rank and file all plowed without needing to be urged on, so that in the end there was no uncultivated land in the wilds and the army had surplus grain. These are all cases that were put into practice and proved effective—how could the ancient methods ultimately be difficult to restore?

As for the garrison and defense troops in Western Shu 西蜀 [Sichuan], they are spread out like stars in the sky or pieces on a chessboard. Every year they require a provisioning quota of several hundred thousand, for which they all depend on supplies from neighboring provinces. The distant roads are rugged and steep, making transport and supply exceedingly difficult; this is not a long-term policy for enduring stability. If one were truly to take the long view in planning and implement the administration of military state farms, could this not reduce the allocations apportioned by the Ministry of Revenue and spare the neighboring provinces the burden of transport and forwarding? You gentlemen observe and weigh the affairs of the times and ought to have insights into this; try to set forth what can be put into practice.

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
問國以民爲本民以食爲天此固無論歲
之豐荒而宜預爲之備者也歲值其豐
有備者固不匱歲值其荒有備者更無
患語荒政於田疇開闢積貯充盈之鄉
深慮者尚爲過計語荒政於天末殘疆
土滿莫耕之區持籌者何得不爲之蚤
計歟考昔荒政十二載在周禮然亦補
救於臨時其先事而爲之備者不恃此
也王制三年耕必有一年之食九年耕
===
必有三年之食以三十年之通雖有凶
旱水溢民無菜色古者有荒歲無荒民
此道得爾西蜀古稱沃野天府之國今
則戶口凋耗井里丘墟間有力耕之處
幸遇有年猶可自給倘豐歉不常倉猝
遘患何以策之則倣古耕九餘三之法
爲重農積粟之計諒不外墾荒以爲備
荒歟惟是語墾荒於蜀中土曠人稀服
田力穡之衆幾何家乎牛種器具之需
punctuated: 問：國以民爲本，民以食爲天，此固無論歲之豐荒而宜預爲之備者也。歲值其豐，有備者固不匱；歲值其荒，有備者更無患。語荒政於田疇開闢、積貯充盈之鄉，深慮者尚爲過計；語荒政於天末殘疆、土滿莫耕之區，持籌者何得不爲之蚤計歟？考昔荒政十二載在《周禮》，然亦補救於臨時，其先事而爲之備者，不恃此也。《王制》：「三年耕必有一年之食，九年耕必有三年之食，以三十年之通，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色。」古者有荒歲無荒民，此道得爾。西蜀古稱沃野、天府之國，今則戶口凋耗，井里丘墟。間有力耕之處，幸遇有年，猶可自給；倘豐歉不常，倉猝遘患，何以策之？則倣古耕九餘三之法，爲重農積粟之計，諒不外墾荒以爲備荒歟？惟是語墾荒於蜀中，土曠人稀，服田力穡之衆幾何家乎？牛種器具之需…
translation_en: Question: The state takes the people as its foundation, and the people take food as their heaven; this is certainly something for which advance preparations should be made, regardless of whether the year's harvest is abundant or poor. When the year happens to be abundant, those who are prepared certainly suffer no scarcity; when the year happens to be one of famine, those who are prepared are even more free from calamity. When speaking of famine-relief administration in regions where fields are opened up for cultivation and stored grain is plentiful, those of deep foresight still make more than ample plans; when speaking of famine-relief administration in a devastated frontier at the ends of the earth, a region where the land is vast yet left unplowed, how could those in charge of planning not calculate early for it? Examining the past, the twelve measures of famine-relief administration are recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), yet they were merely temporary remedies applied when disaster struck; making preparations prior to events did not rely on these. The Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) states: "Three years of plowing must yield one year's surplus of food; nine years of plowing must yield three years' surplus of food. Taking a thirty-year period as the general standard, even if there are disastrous droughts or floods, the people will not have the famished complexion of those eating only wild greens." In antiquity there were years of famine, but no famine-stricken people, because this principle was realized. Western Shu [Sichuan] was in antiquity called a fertile plain and a Land of Heavenly Abundance, yet today its registered population is depleted and its villages lie in ruins. In the few places where strenuous farming takes place, if they are fortunate enough to meet with a good harvest, they can still support themselves; if abundance and scarcity are irregular and they suddenly encounter disaster, by what policy can it be met? Then, to imitate the ancient method of plowing for nine years to have a three-year surplus, and to devise a plan for emphasizing agriculture and storing grain, surely this lies in nothing other than reclaiming wasteland as a means of preparing against famine? Yet when speaking of reclaiming wasteland in Shu, where the land is vast and the people are few, how many households are there among the multitude who work the fields and toil at the harvest? The needed oxen, seed, and implements—…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
從何出乎未集之流移何道以招徠之
現在之土著何術以撫綏之使墾荒有
法而救荒卽不患無策歟他若常平義
倉社倉昔人良法亦可兼舉而行之歟
况爾蜀士荒殘情形
聖天子眷焉西顧久深軫恤
詔旨屢頒懸招民之賞格寛起科之年限免續
墾勸墾之田糧
廟堂之上所以爲蜀民計者至詳且厚總欲其
===
荒蕪闢而生聚繁使豐凶有備而幹止
永寧也爾多士生長斯土留心桑梓未
雨綢繆應蚤爲計之矣尚條晰以陳
punctuated: 從何出乎？未集之流移，何道以招徠之？現在之土著，何術以撫綏之？使墾荒有法，而救荒卽不患無策歟？他若常平、義倉、社倉，昔人良法，亦可兼舉而行之歟？况爾蜀士荒殘情形，聖天子眷焉西顧，久深軫恤，詔旨屢頒，懸招民之賞格，寛起科之年限，免續墾、勸墾之田糧，廟堂之上所以爲蜀民計者，至詳且厚，總欲其荒蕪闢而生聚繁，使豐凶有備而幹止永寧也。爾多士生長斯土，留心桑梓，未雨綢繆，應蚤爲計之矣，尚條晰以陳。
translation_en:
…where are they to come from? By what way may the displaced people who have not yet gathered be drawn back? By what method may the native inhabitants now present be pacified and comforted? If there is a proper method for reclaiming wasteland, will there then be no need to worry about lacking a policy for famine relief? As for other measures such as the Ever-Normal Granaries (changpingcang), Charity Granaries (yicang), and Community Granaries (shecang)—excellent methods of men of the past—can they also be jointly instituted and put into practice?

Moreover, regarding the devastated and desolate condition of your land of Shu (Sichuan), the Sacred Son of Heaven looks withsolicitude toward the west and has long felt deep compassion. Imperial decrees have been repeatedly promulgated, posting reward scales for recruiting settlers, extending the time limits before land is assessed for taxation, and granting exemptions from land tax on newly and encouraged reclamations. What the court above has planned on behalf of the people of Shu is most detailed and generous; overall, it desires that the wastelands be opened up and the population grow and prosper, so that there is preparedness in both good and bad harvests and the people's dwellings and livelihoods enjoy lasting peace. You many scholars were born and raised in this land and take an interest in your native communities; taking precautions before the rain falls, you ought to have planned for this early on. Pray set forth your views item by item with clarity.

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
言寡尤行寡悔祿在其中矣
高之霦
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閱〕薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批〕〔風度端凝〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭茂泰批〔高朗軒豁〕
言行修而祿因之益知學之宜專矣蓋學以爲
言行非以爲祿也乃尤悔寡而祿在焉張也何
===
外求爲且吾人生平所內謀者祗此一二事而
或則馳情於外慕焉亦未嘗返求而審其相因
之報也蓋內之無過於身者外之乃可有用於
世所爲學成於已而天下求之不相及而若相
及也已言行之學亦旣於寡尤寡悔者詳矣處
士恥虛聲而修詞樹德寤寐恒有難慊之隱王
朝崇實學而敷奏明試車服從無濫及之恩在
學者於此亦特難其言之寡尤焉爾修之家者
此言獻之廷者亦此言無論畢生兢業不敢少
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「言寡尤，行寡悔，祿在其中矣。」
高之霦
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閱〕薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批〕〔風度端凝〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭茂泰批〔高朗軒豁〕

言行修而祿因之，益知學之宜專矣。蓋學以爲言行，非以爲祿也。乃尤悔寡而祿在焉，張也何外求爲？且吾人生平所內謀者，祗此一二事，而或則馳情於外慕焉，亦未嘗返求而審其相因之報也。蓋內之無過於身者，外之乃可有用於世，所爲學成於已而天下求之，不相及而若相及也已。言行之學，亦旣於寡尤寡悔者詳矣。處士恥虛聲，而修詞樹德，寤寐恒有難慊之隱；王朝崇實學，而敷奏明試，車服從無濫及之恩。在學者於此，亦特難其言之寡尤焉爾。修之家者此言，獻之廷者亦此言，無論畢生兢業，不敢少
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books
"When one's words give few occasions for blame, and one's actions give few occasions for regret, emolument is therein."
By Gao Zhibin 高之霦
Recommended by Associate Examiner Zhang Yuanke 章元科, District Magistrate of Suiyang County 〔read by Yuanke〕.
Examiner Tu Quan 涂銓, Secretary in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War, assigned to the Capture Supervising Office 〔comment by Quan〕: 〔Dignified and composed in bearing.〕
Comment by Examiner Guo Maotai 郭茂泰, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites: 〔Lofty, clear, and open-minded.〕

When words and actions are cultivated and emolument follows from them, one knows all the more that learning ought to be focused. For learning is pursued for the sake of words and actions, not for the sake of emolument. Yet when blame and regret are few, emolument is found therein—why then should Zizhang 子張 (Zhang 張) seek it outside? Moreover, what we plan for inwardly throughout our lives is merely these one or two matters; if someone lets his feelings race after external desires, it is because he has never turned inward to examine the corresponding recompense that follows from them. For only when inwardly there is no fault in one's person can one outwardly be of use to the world. This is what is meant by learning being brought to completion within oneself and the world then seeking one out—things that do not seem connected and yet are as if connected. The learning of words and actions has already been set forth in detail regarding giving few occasions for blame and regret. A scholar in retirement is ashamed of an empty reputation, and in cultivating his words and establishing his virtue, awake or asleep he constantly harbors a secret uneasiness that is hard to satisfy; the royal court esteems substantial learning, and in receiving reports of words and clearly testing by deeds, the grace of chariots and robes is never bestowed indiscriminately. For the learner in this regard, the particular difficulty lies simply in making his words give few occasions for blame. The words cultivated in the home are these very words, and the words presented at court are also these very words; not to mention that throughout one's whole life one is cautious and attentive, not daring to slightly…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
安也即至一言之獲咎亦以議吾學之疎尤豈
在多乎茲之致謹於言者其前此矣斯言無玷
可免起羞之虞向之幾幾乎期其寡尤而未敢
必其寡尤者今乃得共信曰言寡尤也迨至寡
尤而治言之學全矣又特難其行之寡悔焉耳
措諸躬者此行升諸國者亦此行無論終身懟
遺不敢稍寛也即至一行之負疚亦以貽吾學
之耻悔豈在大乎茲之勉力於行者已有素矣
懿行無斁寧有難白之處向之凜凜乎不敢必
===
其寡悔而又甚期其寡悔者今乃得自信曰行
寡悔也迨至寡悔而制行之學盡矣若此者物
恒僉懟原無糞倖功名之思樞機交飭已裕國
家敬求之本何必言祿也然亦何必不言祿也
天下無因之獲在世或有其過在我正不可存
其心故時而祿至業無負於天子時而祿不必
至學亦無愧於聖賢而况藏修既裕朝廷斷無
負士之理乎是以投之意外適得之意中也往
往然爾吾儒不爽之報在我既盡其實在世寧
punctuated: 安也，即至一言之獲咎，亦以議吾學之疎，尤豈在多乎？茲之致謹於言者，其前此矣。斯言無玷，可免起羞之虞。向之幾幾乎期其寡尤、而未敢必其寡尤者，今乃得共信曰：「言寡尤也。」迨至寡尤，而治言之學全矣。又特難其行之寡悔焉耳。措諸躬者此行，升諸國者亦此行。無論終身懟遺不敢稍寛也，即至一行之負疚，亦以貽吾學之耻，悔豈在大乎？茲之勉力於行者，已有素矣。懿行無斁，寧有難白之處？向之凜凜乎不敢必其寡悔、而又甚期其寡悔者，今乃得自信曰：「行寡悔也。」迨至寡悔，而制行之學盡矣。若此者，物恒僉懟，原無糞倖功名之思；樞機交飭，已裕國家敬求之本。何必言祿也？然亦何必不言祿也？天下無因之獲，在世或有其過，在我正不可存其心。故時而祿至，業無負於天子；時而祿不必至，學亦無愧於聖賢。而况藏修既裕，朝廷斷無負士之理乎？是以投之意外，適得之意中也，往往然爾。吾儒不爽之報，在我既盡其實，在世寧…
translation_en: …at ease, even if a single word incurs blame, it will bring criticism upon the laxity of one's learning—does blame require many words? Here, one's exercise of caution in speech has already been established beforehand. When these words are without blemish, one is spared the anxiety of inviting disgrace. Whereas previously one earnestly hoped to make few occasions for blame without daring to be certain of doing so, now all can believe and say: "His words give few occasions for blame." Once one reaches the point of giving few occasions for blame, the learning of governing speech is complete. And what is especially difficult for him is to have few occasions for regret in his conduct. What is practiced in his own person is this conduct, and what is presented to the state is also this conduct. Not to mention that throughout his life he guards against faults and omissions [?] without daring to be the least bit lenient—even if a single deed brings guilt, it will leave a stain of shame upon his learning; does regret require great matters? Here, his diligent effort in conduct has long been cultivated. When admirable deeds are pursued without weariness, how could there be anything difficult to vindicate? Whereas previously he was filled with awe, not daring to be certain of having few regrets while yet deeply hoping for few regrets, now he can have confidence in himself and say: "My conduct gives few occasions for regret." Once one reaches the point of having few regrets, the learning of regulating conduct is exhausted. Being such as this, in normal affairs all are satisfied [?], and he originally harbors no thought of僥倖 [?] seeking official honors by chance; with the springs of speech and action mutually disciplined, he has already enriched the foundation for the state's respectful search for talent. Why must one speak of emolument? Yet why must one not speak of emolument? As for unearned gains in the world, the world may commit such errors, but within oneself one must never harbor such a mind. Therefore, when at times emolument comes, one's achievements do not fail the Son of Heaven; when at times emolument does not necessarily come, one's learning still has nothing to be ashamed of before the sages and worthies. How much more so when one's private cultivation is already abundant, and the court certainly has no principle for failing a scholar? Thus what is cast beyond one's expectations happens to be obtained within one's intentions; it is often so. As for the unfailing recompense of us Confucians, since within ourselves we have already fulfilled the reality, in the world how could we…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
患無其名故祿之未得也泌水儲公輔之謀猷
祿之已得也廟堂仰眞儒之事功而況內求巳
畜身世並無遺憾之端乎是以取之若寄仍視
之如遺也又往往然爾祿在其中此固言行自
致之符師亦學爲寡尤寡悔而可哉乃知學以
用世者爲大而先以自修者爲眞天下後世之
學者可知所重矣
體羣臣則士之報禮重　　　　雷弘震
===
同考試官眉縣知縣房星著閱　薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂　銓批〔力大思深〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭茂泰批〔容與安詳〕
觀所以報禮者而知體之不容巳也夫體羣臣
君固巳先重夫士矣而報禮斯重焉體之之效
何如哉告公曰君臣之際非可以報稱言也乃
隆以聖主之優恤而百爾之感恩思奮者爲倍
摯焉葢朝廷惟百職爲較踈誠一人無異視之
心斯庶司有必盡之忱則文武之著其經於羣
punctuated:
患無其名？故祿之未得也，泌水儲公輔之謀猷；祿之已得也，廟堂仰眞儒之事功。而況內求巳畜，身世並無遺憾之端乎？是以取之若寄，仍視之如遺也，又往往然爾。「祿在其中」，此固言行自致之符，師亦學爲寡尤、寡悔而可哉！乃知學以用世者爲大，而先以自修者爲眞，天下後世之學者，可知所重矣。

體羣臣則士之報禮重　　　　雷弘震
同考試官眉縣知縣房星著閱　薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂　銓批〔力大思深〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭茂泰批〔容與安詳〕

translation_en:
…worry about lacking its reputation? Therefore, before an emolument is obtained, by the Bi River one stores up the counsel and plans of a ducal minister; once an emolument has been obtained, the court looks up to the achievements and service of a true Confucian. And how much more so when, having sought within and already accumulated virtue, there is no cause for regret in either one's personal life or one's relation to the world? Thus, taking it as though it were merely a temporary lodging, and still regarding it as something left behind—this, too, is very often the case. "Emolument is found therein": this is assuredly the tally naturally brought about by one's words and conduct. Let Zi-zhang [師, i.e. Zizhang 子張] simply learn to make few his faults and few his regrets, and that will suffice! Thus we know that while learning is great insofar as it is of service to the world, it is authentic only when it puts self-cultivation first. Scholars of the empire and of future generations may hereby know where to place their emphasis.

"When he treats the body of officers with sympathetic consideration, the return of礼 [courtesy/service] which the officers make is heavy." — Lei Hongzhen 雷弘震

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
臣者固非爲之而無其效也經言體羣臣矣夫
羣臣固士也立朝端之中被以大君之軫恤而
不生其感慕者當非臣子之心矣列班聯之內
加以我后之推置而不篤其忠貞者諒非人臣
之誼矣乃臣思文武之世優崇不遺於百職恩
意下逮乎羣工其時莫不奔走而禦侮焉莫不
竭智而効忠焉報禮何重也夫亦曰體之爾君
特不體羣臣爾體羣臣則士之報禮不重乎忠
愛原臣子之素志苐無以恤之未能遂大其生
===
成之感爾乃體之者旣至將此日之士咸謂朝
廷之禮何其厚臣子之報何敢輕報以忠貞而
幽獨無欺報以職業而靖共匪懈公忘私而國
忘家者孰不倍切也歟篤棐原人臣之隱念苐
無以動之未能遂作其高厚之戴爾乃體之者
旣切將爾日之士皆謂君上之禮何其隆人臣
之報何敢薄報在一日而矢誠自矢報在百年
而勤勞罔恤內盡忠而外盡職者疇不獨至也
歟雖大君一體之懷原未嘗有責報之意乃君
punctuated: 臣者，固非爲之而無其效也。經言體羣臣矣。夫羣臣固士也。立朝端之中，被以大君之軫恤，而不生其感慕者，當非臣子之心矣；列班聯之內，加以我后之推置，而不篤其忠貞者，諒非人臣之誼矣。乃臣思文、武之世，優崇不遺於百職，恩意下逮乎羣工，其時莫不奔走而禦侮焉，莫不竭智而効忠焉。報禮何重也！夫亦曰體之爾。君特不體羣臣爾；體羣臣，則士之報禮不重乎？忠愛原臣子之素志，苐無以恤之，未能遂大其生成之感爾。乃體之者旣至，將此日之士咸謂朝廷之禮何其厚，臣子之報何敢輕！報以忠貞而幽獨無欺，報以職業而靖共匪懈，公忘私而國忘家者，孰不倍切也歟？篤棐原人臣之隱念，苐無以動之，未能遂作其高厚之戴爾。乃體之者旣切，將爾日之士皆謂君上之禮何其隆，人臣之報何敢薄！報在一日而矢誠自矢，報在百年而勤勞罔恤，內盡忠而外盡職者，疇不獨至也歟？雖大君一體之懷，原未嘗有責報之意；乃君
translation_en: … crowd of officials was surely not practiced without effect. The standard speaks of showing consideration for the crowd of officials. Now, the crowd of officials are indeed scholars. Standing amidst the court and receiving the great sovereign's compassionate care, yet failing to give rise to gratitude and admiration—surely that is not the heart of a subject and son! Ranked within the court rows and accorded our sovereign's trust and placement, yet failing to deepen their loyalty and integrity—surely that is not the duty of a minister! Now I reflect upon the age of Kings Wen and Wu: generous esteem did not overlook the hundred offices, and gracious intent reached down to all the officials. At that time, there were none who did not hasten about to ward off insult, and none who did not exhaust their wisdom to render loyalty. How weighty was their repayment of courtesy! Yet this too was simply a matter of showing consideration for them. A ruler merely fails to show consideration for the crowd of officials; if he shows consideration for the crowd of officials, then will not the scholars' repayment of courtesy be weighty? Loyalty and affection are originally the abiding aspiration of a subject and son; it is only that without anything to show them compassion, one cannot thereby magnify their gratitude for being given life and nourishment. Yet once consideration for them reaches the utmost, the scholars of this day will all say: "How generous is the courtesy of the court! How dare the repayment of a subject and son be slight?" Repaying with loyalty and integrity so that there is no deception even in unseen solitude, repaying through their official duties so that they quietly and恭敬ly serve without laxity—putting the public before the private and the state before the family—who among them would not feel this doubly keenly? Steadfast assistance is originally the innermost thought of a minister; it is only that without anything to move them, one cannot thereby rouse their gratitude for heaven-high and earth-thick grace. Yet once consideration for them becomes earnest, the scholars of that day will all say: "How exalted is the courtesy of the sovereign above! How dare the repayment of a minister be meager?" title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
未嘗責報而臣之報之者無窮良由待之者有
素而應之者自摯也所以聖王之朝凡列庶職
莫不感恩遇而爲國家効一日之職守豈周恤
旣至而猶有不思仰答之臣儕也哉抑人主同
體之意原未嘗有望其卽報之思乃上未嘗卽
望其報而臣之報之者無盡良由馭之者有道
而被之者自切也所以郅隆之代凡厥有位莫
不慕德意而爲王朝殫畢世之圖謀豈主眷旣
隆而尚有不思上酬之臣心也哉而子庶民之
===
效又可詳矣
民日遷善而不知爲之者
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章元科閱　薦
高之霖
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂　銓批　〔神韻高超〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭茂泰批　〔一泓清秀〕
觀遷善之民情益見王道之大也甚矣遷善者
民而爲之者非民也王民竟不之知焉不益見
皡皡之象乎孟子意謂人主出治而不能使一
punctuated:
未嘗責報，而臣之報之者無窮，良由待之者有素，而應之者自摯也。所以聖王之朝，凡列庶職，莫不感恩遇而爲國家効一日之職守，豈周恤旣至，而猶有不思仰答之臣儕也哉！抑人主同體之意，原未嘗有望其卽報之思，乃上未嘗卽望其報，而臣之報之者無盡，良由馭之者有道，而被之者自切也。所以郅隆之代，凡厥有位，莫不慕德意而爲王朝殫畢世之圖謀，豈主眷旣隆，而尚有不思上酬之臣心也哉！而子庶民之效，又可詳矣。

translation_en:
… do not boast to one another. Where for a hundred years there is the blessing of delighting in goodness, for not even a single day is there any trace of yielding credit for goodness. Advancing toward goodness day by day, those who turn to the Supreme Standard offer no praise for the august plans. How then could there be anyone praying for the great sovereign or singing his praises?

At this I almost suspect that the true king's people are simple-minded. For when even a single good policy or a single good ordinance moves people to unceasing praise, how much more so with one who shares in goodness like a true king—how could they be oblivious to whence it comes? Yet in those days, when the true king perfected customs, he made people neither fear him nor yearn after him. Those born in his era saw every household ascend to benevolence and longevity, utterly without selfish prayers or eulogies. Precisely because of their simple-mindedness did they become the people of a true king, and nothing more.

At this I also admire the unadorned simplicity of the true king's people. For when goodness extends to a single person or to several people, it stirs others to endless acclaim; how much more so with actions of shared goodness like those of a true king—how could they completely forget how it was brought about? Yet in those days, when the true king made the people sincere, families had no differing teachings and the state shared the same customs. Those who followed that age saw customs reach pure and generous simplicity, swiftly erasing any look of agitation or boasting. Precisely because of their unadorned simplicity did they become the contented and self-possessed people of a true king, and nothing more.

Yet having broadly observed the feelings of the people, one ought all the more to seek deeply into the ruler's virtue; therefore, one goes further to reflect upon the noble man.

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
者其極耳庶民於極之敷言何如乎極本於皇
而於言焉敷之是言也葢天子光被之道德所
煥而頒之者也使庶民於此而不深其諷咏不
篤其遵循不幾與天子相遠而何能近其光華
哉乃庶民則已是訓矣厥居之理自在人心而
一經天子之開導遂覺其可歌而可傳以爲此
天子之教我良厚也一日之誦說維是終身之
念典亦惟是不於是訓而何訓乎此其諷咏誠
深矣且不惟是訓也而又是行矣彛倫之則人
===
生大共而一聞天子之敷陳遂覺其可法而可
守以爲此天子之惠我誠至也一人之體備者
在是人人之踐履者亦在是不於是行而何行
乎此其遵循已篤矣夫民亦特慮其訓行之無
自爾今旣如是其訓也如是其行也謂僅是庶
民之會極乎庶民之歸極乎所以近天子之光
者卽在是矣天子首庶民而垂型卽統庶民而
觀化光輝之發越非絶人以難企也若玆之鼓
舞不倦庶民豈有扞格之慮乎通作君於作師
punctuated: 者，其極耳。庶民於極之敷言何如乎？極本於皇，而於言焉敷之。是言也，葢天子光被之道德所煥而頒之者也。使庶民於此而不深其諷咏、不篤其遵循，不幾與天子相遠，而何能近其光華哉？乃庶民則已是訓矣。厥居之理自在人心，而一經天子之開導，遂覺其可歌而可傳，以爲此天子之教我良厚也。一日之誦說維是，終身之念典亦惟是，不於是訓而何訓乎？此其諷咏誠深矣。且不惟是訓也，而又是行矣。彛倫之則，人生大共，而一聞天子之敷陳，遂覺其可法而可守，以爲此天子之惠我誠至也。一人之體備者在是，人人之踐履者亦在是，不於是行而何行乎？此其遵循已篤矣。夫民亦特慮其訓行之無自爾。今旣如是其訓也，如是其行也，謂僅是庶民之會極乎？庶民之歸極乎？所以近天子之光者，卽在是矣。天子首庶民而垂型，卽統庶民而觀化。光輝之發越，非絶人以難企也。若玆之鼓舞不倦，庶民豈有扞格之慮乎？通作君於作師，
translation_en:
…is simply the Supreme Standard itself. How, then, do the common people respond to the widely diffused words of the Supreme Standard? The Supreme Standard originates with the August Sovereign, and through words it is diffused. These words are indeed that which the resplendent morality of the Son of Heaven illuminates and promulgates. If the common people, in regard to this, did not deepen their recitation and chanting of them, and did not make earnest their adherence to them, would they not become estranged from the Son of Heaven, and how could they draw near to his glorious splendor? 

Yet the common people already take these words as their instruction! The principles of their station naturally reside within the human heart, and once guided by the Son of Heaven, they immediately feel that these words are worthy of being sung and transmitted, considering that the Son of Heaven's instruction of them is truly generous. What is recited for a single day is this; what is cherished as a canon for a whole lifetime is also this alone. If they do not take this as their instruction, what else should they take as instruction? In this, their recitation and chanting are truly deep. 

Moreover, they not only take this as their instruction, they also put this into practice! The rules of normal human relationships are shared in common by all human life, and once they hear the Son of Heaven's setting forth of them, they immediately feel that these are worthy of being modeled upon and upheld, considering that the Son of Heaven's grace toward them is truly supreme. What is embodied in completeness by the One Man lies in this, and what is put into practice by every person also lies in this. If they do not put this into practice, what else should they put into practice? In this, their adherence is already earnest. 

Now, one might only worry that the people have no way to receive instruction and put it into practice. Now that they are instructed in it like this, and put it into practice like this, can this be called merely the common people's coming together at the Supreme Standard, or the common people's returning to the Supreme Standard? The means by which they draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven lies right here! The Son of Heaven stands at the head of the common people to hand down a model, and thereby governs the common people to observe their transformation. The radiance of his glory does not cut people off by being impossible to reach. With such untiring encouragement and inspiration as this, how could the common people have any worry of obstruction or resistance? Integrating the role of ruler with the role of teacher…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
異也然使勤於始者怠於終則儀釆未見增華
何以著飲食中心之願歷都會而切伊人之慕
其再覩之干旟又然也然使殷於再者疎於後
則物色猶然如故何以昭式廬下士之忱而大
夫不然也彼孑孑干旌則又在浚之城矣以旌
之麗於干也草野屬耳目焉等威之制宜爾也
是旌非大夫所同有者哉今何以同有之旌忽
若爲獨有之旌也覽國門之在望覺旌之增輝
於浚者良多已以干之係夫旌也閭里肅觀瞻
===
焉文物之建應然也是旌非吾儕所習見者哉
今何以習見之旌偏若爲創見之旌也覩雉堞
之當前覺旌之榮施於浚者良深已是葢有結
契於干旌之先者矣昔不過三命之恒儀今則
爲一時之曠典想大夫綢繆雅誼有掩映於翟
羽之旁者而玆特呈其象也不令人欽夫三接
之勤也哉是葢有神馳於浚城之外者矣昔則
簡出於深居今忽貴臨於下邑想大夫勸駕情
殷必有隱寓於旟章之表者而玆特昭其釆也
punctuated: 異也。然使勤於始者怠於終，則儀釆未見增華，何以著飲食中心之願？歷都會而切伊人之慕，其再覩之干旟又然也。然使殷於再者疎於後，則物色猶然如故，何以昭式廬下士之忱？而大夫不然也。彼孑孑干旌，則又在浚之城矣。以旌之麗於干也，草野屬耳目焉，等威之制宜爾也。是旌非大夫所同有者哉？今何以同有之旌，忽若爲獨有之旌也？覽國門之在望，覺旌之增輝於浚者良多已。以干之係夫旌也，閭里肅觀瞻焉，文物之建應然也。是旌非吾儕所習見者哉？今何以習見之旌，偏若爲創見之旌也？覩雉堞之當前，覺旌之榮施於浚者良深已。是葢有結契於干旌之先者矣。昔不過三命之恒儀，今則爲一時之曠典。想大夫綢繆雅誼，有掩映於翟羽之旁者，而玆特呈其象也，不令人欽夫三接之勤也哉？是葢有神馳於浚城之外者矣。昔則簡出於深居，今忽貴臨於下邑。想大夫勸駕情殷，必有隱寓於旟章之表者，而玆特昭其釆也，
translation_en:
…different. Yet if one who was diligent at the beginning grew lax at the end, and the splendor of his trappings showed no added brilliance, how could he manifest the heartfelt desire of his hospitality? Passing into the metropolis and feeling an earnest longing for "that man," the pole and falcon-banner seen a second time were likewise so. Yet if one who was ardent a second time became neglectful thereafter, and the external array remained merely as before, how could he display the sincerity of bowing from his carriage to a humble cottage and humbling himself before scholars?

Yet the grand masters are not like this! Those conspicuous staff-banners are now at the city wall of Xun! Because the feathered banner is attached to the staff, the eyes and ears of the rustic countryside are fixed upon it; the system of hierarchical majesty requires that it be so. Are these banners not something held in common by all grand masters? Why is it that today, a banner held in common suddenly seems like a banner uniquely possessed? Gazing at the capital gate within sight, one feels that the radiance the banners add to Xun is great indeed. Because the staff is bound with the feathered banner, the village lanes look upon it with solemn reverence; the establishment of ritual emblems ought to be so. Are these banners not something we are accustomed to seeing? Why is it that today, a familiar banner seems instead like a banner seen for the very first time? Beholding the crenellated battlements right before us, one feels that the honor the banners bestow upon Xun is deep indeed.

This is because there was already a bond of affinity formed prior to the arrival of the staff-banners. What in the past was no more than the routine insignia of a thrice-commissioned official has today become an extraordinary ceremony of the age. One imagines that the grand master's closely bound, refined friendship is gleaming beside the pheasant feathers, and here it merely manifests its outward image—does it not make people admire the diligence of his thrice-repeated receptions? This is also because his spirit had already sped beyond the city wall of Xun. Whereas in the past he rarely ventured out from his secluded residence, today he suddenly honors a humble town with his noble presence. One imagines that the grand master's earnest affection in urging the worthy to mount his carriage must be subtly lodged beyond the emblazoned banners, and here it merely displays its outward splendor—…

殫厥心而漫云靖獻者也葢無可諉者大臣之
職而有必盡者大臣之心惟盡其必欲盡之心
而此心可無媿者厥職亦以無曠耳山甫之盡

text:
匪解以事一人乎邦國治安之策一人每以其
任寄之元老謂其鞠躬盡瘁貞常變而一致耳
今觀山甫洵有然也才大而爵之以養功高而
守之以謙兢兢然夙夜罔逸祗求無所怠於事
之中不敢有所希於事之外以是而言篤棐篤
棐爲已深矣邦國久大之謨一人多以其事委
之碩德謂其盡力翊贊歷始終而罔渝耳今觀

===
事並不敢有要結於一人之心以是而言靖共
靖共爲已至矣在山甫本小心翼翼之衷作王
朝股肱之良初何嘗自謂其匪解乃匪解之心
固可從令儀色而式古訓者想見之也即此寅
恭永篤我知其鐘鼎之底定於無疆也哉抑山
甫以柔嘉維則之範膺天室冢宰之任又何嘗
自知其匪解乃匪解之心固可從若天子而賦
明命者驗之也即此忠貞無替我知其世曆之
永綿於未艾也哉山甫洵足美矣
punctuated: 匪解，以事一人乎！邦國治安之策，一人每以其任寄之元老，謂其鞠躬盡瘁，貞常變而一致耳。今觀山甫，洵有然也。才大而爵之以養，功高而守之以謙，兢兢然夙夜罔逸，祗求無所怠於事之中，不敢有所希於事之外，以是而言篤棐，篤棐爲已深矣。邦國久大之謨，一人多以其事委之碩德，謂其盡力翊贊，歷始終而罔渝耳。今觀山甫，洵若是也。位尊而處之以卑，學廣而返之於約，凜凜然夙夜不遑，惟所無玩忽於一人之事，並不敢有要結於一人之心，以是而言靖共，靖共爲已至矣。在山甫本小心翼翼之衷，作王朝股肱之良，初何嘗自謂其匪解？乃匪解之心，固可從令儀色而式古訓者想見之也。即此寅恭永篤，我知其鐘鼎之底定於無疆也哉！抑山甫以柔嘉維則之範，膺天室冢宰之任，又何嘗自知其匪解？乃匪解之心，固可從若天子而賦明命者驗之也。即此忠貞無替，我知其世曆之永綿於未艾也哉！山甫洵足美矣。
translation_en: …never slacken, in order to serve the One Man!” For policies of peace and order in the state, the One Man always entrusts the responsibility to his senior statesmen, reckoning that they will bend their backs and exhaust their strength, remaining steadfast and consistent through both normal times and crises. Now, looking at Shanfu, he truly was like this. Though his talent was great, he tempered it with cultivation [? 爵之以養]; though his achievements were lofty, he maintained them with humility. Cautious and wary, day and night without taking ease, he sought only to avoid any negligence within his duties, and dared not harbor any ambitions beyond his duties. Speaking of his devoted assistance in this light, his devoted assistance was profound indeed. For far-reaching and great counsels of the state, the One Man mostly delegates the affairs to men of eminent virtue, reckoning that they will spare no effort in assisting and supporting him, never changing from beginning to end. Now, looking at Shanfu, he truly was so. Though his position was exalted, he abided in it with lowliness; though his learning was broad, he brought it back to essentials. Awed and trembling, day and night without leisure, he sought only [惟所, perhaps for 惟求] to avoid any trifling or neglect in the affairs of the One Man, and furthermore dared not harbor any intent to curry favor with the heart of the One Man. Speaking of his quiet devotion to duty in this light, his quiet devotion was supreme indeed. As for Shanfu, grounding himself in a heart of reverent caution to act as a worthy right-hand minister of the royal court, when did he ever claim for himself that he never slackened? Yet his unslackening heart can surely be envisioned from the way he perfected his deportment and countenance and took ancient precepts as his model. By this very reverence and respect ever deeply maintained, I know that his merit inscribed on bells and tripods was established without bound! Or again, when Shanfu, with his model of gentle goodness as the rule, bore the office of Prime Minister (Zhongzai) of the heavenly house, when did he ever know of himself that he never slackened? Yet his unslackening heart can surely be verified from the way he obeyed the Son of Heaven and spread abroad the bright mandate. By this very loyalty and constancy never failing, I know that the succession of his house’s years was prolonged forever without end! Shanfu is truly worthy of praise.

康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
宣公元年
曾　亮
同考試官峩眉縣知縣房〔星著〕閱　薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂　銓批　瑩徹
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰〕批　整練
於帥師師者謹其微而著其美者亦見矣此棐林
之師不書趙盾恐臣疑於君也若夫地而後伐
又何得以同詞例乎是可以知聖人之意矣今
===
夫聖人一載筆間凡所以正綱常別同異者其
旨固甚精微也故事有分別而始見者不有以
別之恐其失所辨亦有不必分別而始見者過
有以別之恐又至於淆後之學者讀其書思其
義亦可以知聖人載筆之意矣如春秋書棐林
之役可觀焉夫兵衆則曰師師者因其衆而名
之者也乃有以為大趙盾之事而稱師者無亦
未明於聖人之旨也哉夫師衆而將卑則稱師
師少而將尊則稱將將尊師衆僉書於策者春
punctuated:
「宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。」（宣公元年）
曾　亮
同考試官、峩眉縣知縣房〔星著〕閱，薦。
考試官、兵部職方司督捕主事涂　銓批：「瑩徹。」
考試官、禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰〕批：「整練。」

於帥師師者謹其微，而著其美者亦見矣。此棐林之師不書趙盾，恐臣疑於君也。若夫地而後伐，又何得以同詞例乎？是可以知聖人之意矣。今夫聖人一載筆間，凡所以正綱常、別同異者，其旨固甚精微也。故事有分別而始見者，不有以別之，恐其失所辨；亦有不必分別而始見者，過有以別之，恐又至於淆。後之學者讀其書，思其義，亦可以知聖人載筆之意矣，如《春秋》書棐林之役可觀焉。夫兵衆則曰「師」，師者因其衆而名之者也。乃有以為大趙盾之事而稱「師」者，無亦未明於聖人之旨也哉？夫師衆而將卑則稱「師」，師少而將尊則稱將，將尊、師衆僉書於策者，《春
translation_en:
"The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng" (First Year of Duke Xuan).

Zeng Liang 曾亮.
Read and recommended by Associate Examiner Fang Xingzhu 房星著, Magistrate of Emei County.
Evaluated by Examiner Tu Quan 涂銓, Secretary for Capturing Fugitives in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War, with the comment: "Luminous and penetrating."
Evaluated by Examiner Guo Maotai 郭茂泰, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies of the Ministry of Rites, with the comment: "Well-ordered and polished."

In taking caution with the subtle implications concerning the commander of the army [?], the manifestation of what is admirable in the expedition is also made visible. That this army at Feilin does not record the name of Zhao Dun 趙盾 is out of fear that a subject might be confused in status with a ruler. As for naming the place first and only afterward recording the attack, how could that be interpreted according to the precedent of identical phrasing? From this one may understand the intention of the Sage.

Now, whenever the Sage set brush to record, in all whereby he rectified the cardinal principles and constant virtues and distinguished similarities and differences, his underlying import was assuredly most subtle and refined. Therefore, there are matters whose meaning becomes apparent only when a distinction is drawn; if one does not distinguish them, there is the fear that the point of differentiation will be lost. Yet there are also matters whose meaning is already apparent without needing to draw a distinction; if one goes too far in distinguishing them, there is the fear that it will instead lead to confusion. When later scholars read his book and ponder its meaning, they too can understand the intention with which the Sage set down his brush—as may be seen in how the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the campaign at Feilin.

Now, when troops are numerous, they are called an "army" (shi 師); "army" is a designation given on account of their multitude. Yet there are some who suppose that it was called an "army" in order to magnify the enterprise of Zhao Dun—have they not failed to grasp the import of the Sage? That when the troops are numerous and the commander is of low rank, the text records "army"; when the troops are few and the commander is of noble rank, it records the commander; and when both the commander is noble and the troops are numerous, both are recorded together in the annals—this is the rule of the Spring…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
秋之法也試思此舉也帥師者太原之上卿從
行者友邦之侯伯貴乎不貴乎聖人曰以晉大
夫而率率與國之諸侯可也以晉大夫率率與
國之諸侯而貿焉不辨尊卑不可也以諸國而
往從乎晉大夫可也以諸國從晉大夫而茫然
不辨君臣不可也於是書晉師焉寧以師蔽盾
毋以盾蔽君亦若宋陳諸君率率晉陽之士焉
以問罪於鄭者君尊臣卑之分何凜凜歟而或
者曰會而後伐前此嘗譏其疑於義矣夫同爲
===
疑於義之文必同爲疑於義之事正恐棐林之
役幾何不與前之秣義者同類而並譏也若然
是止知有同異之辨不知有異而無嫌於同之
辨也夫事同而文同者因文以求事文同而事
不同者因事而可知其文彼夫聖人寧從同
之義無貴立異之條者學者亦嘗潛心而究其
義乎故善讀經者辨其所當辨而不辨其所不
必辨斯可矣
禮記
punctuated:
秋之法也。試思此舉也，帥師者太原之上卿，從行者友邦之侯伯，貴乎不貴乎？聖人曰：以晉大夫而率率與國之諸侯可也，以晉大夫率率與國之諸侯而貿焉不辨尊卑不可也；以諸國而往從乎晉大夫可也，以諸國從晉大夫而茫然不辨君臣不可也。於是書「晉師」焉，寧以師蔽盾，毋以盾蔽君，亦若宋、陳諸君率率晉陽之士焉以問罪於鄭者，君尊臣卑之分何凜凜歟！而或者曰：「會而後伐，前此嘗譏其疑於義矣。夫同爲疑於義之文，必同爲疑於義之事，正恐棐林之役，幾何不與前之秣義者同類而並譏也。」若然，是止知有同異之辨，不知有異而無嫌於同之辨也。夫事同而文同者，因文以求事；文同而事不同者，因事而可知其文。彼夫聖人寧從同之義，無貴立異之條者，學者亦嘗潛心而究其義乎？故善讀經者，辨其所當辨，而不辨其所不必辨，斯可矣。

禮記
translation_en:
… the rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). Consider this campaign: the one commanding the troops was the Senior Grand Master of Taiyuan [Jin], and those following in the expedition were the marquises and earls of allied states—were they of noble rank or not? The Sage held that for a Grand Master of Jin to lead the feudal lords of allied states was permissible as a fact, but for a Grand Master of Jin to lead the feudal lords of allied states and rashly fail to distinguish between high and low status was impermissible; for the various states to go and follow a Grand Master of Jin was permissible as a fact, but for the various states to follow a Grand Master of Jin and blindly fail to distinguish between ruler and subject was impermissible. Therefore he recorded "the army of Jin," preferring to subsume Zhao Dun under the army rather than let Zhao Dun overshadow the rulers—making it appear as though the rulers of Song, Chen, and the other states were leading the troops of Jinyang to punish Zheng for its crimes. How awe-inspiring is the distinction between the exalted ruler and the lowly subject! Yet someone might say: "Meeting first and then attacking was previously criticized as being doubtful in righteousness. Now, since the wording is identical to that used for cases doubtful in righteousness, it must likewise be an affair doubtful in righteousness; one fears that the campaign at Feilin is almost indistinguishable from those earlier instances that hesitated over [?] righteousness, and is criticized alongside them." If one argues thus, one only knows the distinction between similarity and difference, and does not know the distinction of things being different in nature without any objection to their being recorded in the same way. When the affairs are the same and the wording is the same, one seeks the affair through the wording; when the wording is the same yet the affairs are different, one can understand the wording through the affair itself. As for the Sage preferring to follow the principle of using identical wording rather than valuing the creation of divergent rules, have scholars ever immersed their minds to investigate this meaning? Therefore, those who are skilled at reading the Classics distinguish what ought to be distinguished, and do not distinguish what does not need to be distinguished—and that suffices.

Record of Rites (Liji)

上賢以崇德　　　程鴻
同考試官蒼溪縣知縣賈〔先華閲〕薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事凃　銓批〔秀逸〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批雅馴〕
取士於鄉而野無遺賢已蓋有德乃可爲賢非
上何以爲崇也上以崇之鄉學之取士也有如
此且王者詳於教士未嘗不亟於取士也蓋譽
望之挺生不偶而内美之醇備可風惟卽登進
之典示以優崇之意庶服教者曉然於上意之
所在而朝廷造士之澤至此亦觀其有成也若
禮教若政與道德鄉學教士之法可謂詳矣然
國家養士有年無非欲英才輩出奏庶績之咸
熙則沐浴既久豈無以髦士著稱者出副君相
敬求之意卽司徒董正維殷無非冀多士充廷
作王朝之勵翼則論辯既加又何可以拔擢或
緩者致失德造大成之儒甚矣惟賢有德崇之
宜亟也士以崇之有固然者德爲同然之理何
punctuated:
「上賢以崇德」　　　程鴻
同考試官蒼溪縣知縣賈〔先華閲〕薦。
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事凃〔銓批：秀逸〕。
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批：雅馴〕。
取士於鄉，而野無遺賢已。蓋有德乃可爲賢，非上何以爲崇也？上以崇之，鄉學之取士也有如此。且王者詳於教士，未嘗不亟於取士也。蓋譽望之挺生不偶，而内美之醇備可風。惟卽登進之典，示以優崇之意，庶服教者曉然於上意之所在，而朝廷造士之澤，至此亦觀其有成也。若禮教、若政與道德，鄉學教士之法，可謂詳矣。然國家養士有年，無非欲英才輩出，奏庶績之咸熙。則沐浴既久，豈無以髦士著稱者，出副君相敬求之意？卽司徒董正維殷，無非冀多士充廷，作王朝之勵翼。則論辯既加，又何可以拔擢或緩者，致失德造大成之儒？甚矣，惟賢有德，崇之宜亟也。士以崇之，有固然者。德爲同然之理，何
translation_en:
"Exalting the worthy in order to revere virtue." — Cheng Hong 程鴻

Recommended by Associate Examiner Jia Xianhua 賈先華, Magistrate of Cangxi District 蒼溪縣.
Examiner Tu Quan 凃銓, Secretary for the Capture of Fugitives in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War, comments: "Graceful and spirited."
Examiner Guo Maotai 郭茂泰, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites, comments: "Refined and well-ordered."

When scholars are selected in the rural districts, no worthy men are left neglected in the countryside. Indeed, it is only by possessing virtue that one can be deemed worthy; and without exalting them, how can virtue be revered? By exalting them in order to revere virtue, such is the way the district schools select scholars.

Moreover, while a true king is thorough in educating scholars, he is no less urgent in selecting them. For the emergence of men ofoutstanding reputation is no mere accident, and the pure completeness of their inner excellence can serve as a moral influence. Only by using the very canon of promotion and advancement to manifest the intention of honoring and revering them will those who submit to instruction clearly understand where the sovereign's intention lies, and the court's grace in cultivating scholars will at this point also be seen to reach fulfillment.

Whether through ritual teaching, governance, or moral virtue, the methods by which the district schools educate scholars may be called thorough indeed. Yet when the state nurtures scholars over many years, it desires nothing other than for brilliant talents to emerge in succession and achieve the harmonious flourishing of all official endeavors. Having been steeped in this influence for so long, how could there not be those renowned as eminent scholars who step forth to fulfill the respectful seeking of the ruler and his ministers? Even the Minister of Education (Situ 司徒), so earnest in his supervision and rectification, hopes for nothing other than an abundance of scholars to fill the court and act as encouraging wings to the royal house. Once assessment and evaluation have been applied, how could one allow any delay in their selection and promotion to cause the loss of scholars whose virtue and attainment have reached great completion?

Indeed, because the worthy possess virtue, revering them ought to be urgent; that they are exalted [reading 上 for 士] in order to revere virtue is a matter of course. Virtue is a principle shared by all alike: what …

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
人不宜自淑而一人獨克全罔叙焉賢之所爲
特著也使無以上之何以彰崇奬之有道乎惟
上之而爵祿或難遽及選造有所必先凡以賢
之不壅於上聞卽德之不蔽於庸類也庶天下
共識懿德之尊矣德爲大共之美何人不可自
勉而若人獨克備罔愆焉賢之所由見稱也倘
無以上之何以見崇重之特至乎惟上之而名
器雖不易錫旌揚有所宜加凡以賢之係於國
者重卽以德之彰於賢者至也庶斯世共覩有
===
德之榮矣於此見朝廷用人之效焉選舉之法
未精則登進之途或濫若卽上以爲崇而下無
畱良斯上有國楨有不慶彙征而相策勵也哉
於此見廣勵人材之思焉天下不覩舉賢之典
吾人無以識修德之徵若因崇以爲上而野無
遺美斯朝多修士有不砥實行而礪名節也哉
雖其間或以言揚或以行舉總不殊此薦賢之
至意或升之司徒或升之司馬無非同此彰德
之深心而未已也又有簡不肖之法在
punctuated: 人不宜自淑，而一人獨克全罔叙焉，賢之所爲特著也。使無以上之，何以彰崇奬之有道乎？惟上之，而爵祿或難遽及，選造有所必先，凡以賢之不壅於上聞，卽德之不蔽於庸類也，庶天下共識懿德之尊矣。德爲大共之美，何人不可自勉，而若人獨克備罔愆焉，賢之所由見稱也。倘無以上之，何以見崇重之特至乎？惟上之，而名器雖不易錫，旌揚有所宜加，凡以賢之係於國者重，卽以德之彰於賢者至也，庶斯世共覩有德之榮矣。於此見朝廷用人之效焉。選舉之法未精，則登進之途或濫；若卽上以爲崇，而下無畱良，斯上有國楨，有不慶彙征而相策勵也哉？於此見廣勵人材之思焉。天下不覩舉賢之典，吾人無以識修德之徵；若因崇以爲上，而野無遺美，斯朝多修士，有不砥實行而礪名節也哉？雖其間或以言揚，或以行舉，總不殊此薦賢之至意；或升之司徒，或升之司馬，無非同此彰德之深心。而未已也，又有簡不肖之法在。
translation_en:
…person ought not to cultivate himself in it? Yet when one person alone is able to fulfill it completely and without flaw [?], this is why his worthiness stands out so conspicuously. If there were no way to advance him, how could one display the proper way of honoring and encouraging him? Only by advancing him—so that even if noble rank and emolument cannot immediately reach him, selection and training must take precedence—all so that worthiness is not blocked from being heard above, which means that virtue is not obscured among the common crowd, may the whole world come to recognize the dignity of admirable virtue. Virtue is a universal beauty; what person cannot exert himself in it? Yet when such a person alone is able to possess it fully and without fault, this is why his worthiness comes to be praised. If there were no way to advance him, how could one show the utmost degree of honor and esteem? Only by advancing him—so that even though titles and insignia of office are not lightly bestowed, commendation and praise ought to be conferred—all because the importance of the worthy to the state is weighty, which means that the manifestation of virtue in the worthy reaches the utmost, may this age together behold the glory of possessing virtue.

Herein is seen the efficacy of the court's employment of men. If the methods of selection and recommendation are not refined, the paths of advancement may become indiscriminate; if, however, honoring them consists directly in advancing them, so that no good talent is left behind below, and thus above there are pillars of the state, will men not rejoice in advancing together in categories and mutually spur one another on? Herein is seen the intention of broadly encouraging men of talent. If the world does not witness the statutes for recommending the worthy, people have no way to recognize the proofs of cultivating virtue; if, however, advancing them follows from honoring them, so that no fine talent is overlooked in the countryside, and thus the court is full of cultivated scholars, will men not whet their substantial conduct and hone their integrity and reputation? Although among them some may be exalted for their words and others recommended for their conduct, in sum it does not differ from this utmost intention of recommending the worthy; whether they are promoted to the Minister of Education (situ) or promoted to the Minister of War (sima), none of this is anything other than the same profound mind for making virtue manifest. And it does not stop here; there is also the method of weeding out the unworthy.

text:
樂文同則上下和矣

樂以救禮極之上下而咸和焉夫上下未和以
樂文之未同也文同則上下和又何致生離乎
且從來有品秩以定冠履之分即不可無音節
以聯尊卑之情故其一德相孚畧威嚴而深愛
===
戴者蓋大樂之感召有自而中情之鼓舞甚深
也禮義立則貴賤等禮之救樂有然矣樂寧無
以救禮也哉夫禮之救樂固虞其儀之不肅也
樂之救禮尤虞其志之未孚果何以順成有象
堂簾無隔絕之情抑禮之救樂固患其分之未
嚴也樂之救禮尤患其心之未愜果何以休豫
是昭貴賤有相通之志是貴於樂文之同也樂
文同而上下有不和者乎樂足以統天下之同
而無淪於異亦足以制天下之異而歸於同固
punctuated:
《樂文同則上下和矣》
程鴻
同考試官蒼溪縣知縣賈〔光華〕閱，薦。
