樂以救禮，極之上下而咸和焉。夫上下未和，以樂文之未同也；文同則上下和，又何致生離乎？且從來有品秩以定冠履之分，即不可無音節以聯尊卑之情。故其一德相孚、畧威嚴而深愛戴者，蓋大樂之感召有自，而中情之鼓舞甚深也。「禮義立則貴賤等」，禮之救樂有然矣，樂寧無以救禮也哉？夫禮之救樂，固虞其儀之不肅也；樂之救禮，尤虞其志之未孚。果何以順成有象，堂簾無隔絕之情？抑禮之救樂，固患其分之未嚴也；樂之救禮，尤患其心之未愜。果何以休豫是昭，貴賤有相通之志？是貴於樂文之同也。樂文同，而上下有不和者乎？樂足以統天下之同而無淪於異，亦足以制天下之異而歸於同，固
translation_en:
"When the patterns of music are unified, then superior and inferior are harmonious."
Cheng Hong 程鴻
Read and recommended by Associate Examiner Jia Guanghua 賈光華, Magistrate of Cangxi County.
Comment by Examiner Tu Quan 涂銓, Secretary for the Capture of Fugitives in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War: [Tranquil and far-reaching].
Comment by Examiner Guo Maotai 郭茂泰, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites: [Clear and lustrous].

Music remedies the excesses of ritual, extending all the way to superior and inferior so that all are harmonious. Now, when superior and inferior are not yet harmonious, it is because the patterns of music are not yet unified; when the patterns are unified, superior and inferior are harmonious—how then could estrangement arise? Moreover, ever since there have been ranks and grades to fix the distinction between cap and shoe, there could not fail to be musical rhythms to bind together the feelings of the noble and the base. Therefore, when they trust one another in shared virtue, setting aside stern majesty and deepening affectionate devotion, it is because the inspiring call of great music has its source, and the rousing of inner feelings is profound indeed. "When ritual principles are established, the noble and the base are differentiated"—such is how ritual remedies music; how then could music lack the means to remedy ritual? Now, when ritual remedies music, it certainly guards against ceremonies not being reverent; when music remedies ritual, it especially guards against intentions not yet being in mutual trust. How indeed is the image of harmonious completion achieved, so that there is no feeling of separation between the hall and the screen? Furthermore, when ritual remedies music, it certainly worries that distinctions are not yet strict; when music remedies ritual, it especially worries that hearts are not yet satisfied. How indeed is joyful ease made manifest, so that the noble and the base have mutually communicating aspirations? This depends upon the unification of the patterns of music. When the patterns of music are unified, could superior and inferior ever fail to be harmonious? Music is sufficient to unite the sameness of the world so that it does not sink into difference, and is also sufficient to regulate the differences of the world so that they return to sameness; indeed…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
有篤摯於人情而難已者何其和樂而情情深也
特情文未協上下遂多睽隔耳若異不終異而
有樂以統異凡外之有所殊者皆洽於內之不
可解睽隔之端何自而起歟蓋有交盡其和愜
者矣樂足以化天下之離亦足以合天下之情而不復離固有流貫於人心而莫
解者何其和易而可親也第儀文未調上下遂
致懸殊耳惟離不復離而有樂以制離凡體之
有所隔者皆化於情之無所岐殊絕之象何自
===
而生歟蓋有交致其誠和者矣論大樂之格被
欣喜歡愛之至天地且將訢合焉而況於上下
然不推之上下無以見樂之攸䝉為至深也所
以聖王乂安方夏即在揮絃緼㮣之中論至樂
之感乎和平樂易之極茂植且登咸若焉何況
於上下惟觀之於上下乃以見樂之感通有甚
廣也所以聖王靜一流競恆著干戚羽旄之盛
蓋樂文之同即成不爭之化上下之和悉歸無
怨之休樂之救禮如此
punctuated: 有篤摯於人情而難已者，何其和樂而情情深也！特情文未協，上下遂多睽隔耳。若異不終異，而有樂以統異，凡外之有所殊者，皆洽於內之不可解，睽隔之端，何自而起歟？蓋有交盡其和愜者矣。樂足以化天下之離，亦足以合天下之情而不復離，固有流貫於人心而莫解者，何其和易而可親也！第儀文未調，上下遂致懸殊耳。惟離不復離，而有樂以制離，凡體之有所隔者，皆化於情之無所岐，殊絕之象，何自而生歟？蓋有交致其誠和者矣。論大樂之格被，欣喜歡愛之至，天地且將訢合焉，而況於上下？然不推之上下，無以見樂之攸䝉為至深也。所以聖王乂安方夏，即在揮絃緼㮣之中。論至樂之感乎，和平樂易之極，茂植且登咸若焉，何況於上下？惟觀之於上下，乃以見樂之感通有甚廣也。所以聖王靜一流競，恆著干戚羽旄之盛。蓋樂文之同，即成不爭之化；上下之和，悉歸無怨之休。樂之救禮如此。
translation_en:
…is something deeply sincere in human sentiment that cannot be suppressed—how harmonious, joyful, and profound in feeling [情情, sic] it is! It is only when sentiment and outward form are not yet coordinated that estrangement and division often arise between superiors and inferiors. If differences do not remain differences to the end, and there is music to unify those differences, then everything that is distinct on the outside blends into an inextricable unity on the inside; from where, then, could the beginnings of estrangement and division arise? Indeed, both sides fully realize their harmony and satisfaction.

Music suffices to transform the separations of the world, and it also suffices to unite the sentiments of the world so that they are no longer separated; there is inherently something flowing through human hearts that cannot be untied—how gentle, accessible, and approachable it is! It is only when ceremonial forms are not yet attuned that a wide gulf arises between superiors and inferiors. Only when separation is no longer separation, and there is music to regulate separation, is everything that is divided in status transformed by sentiment without divergence; from where, then, could the signs of wide separation arise? Indeed, both sides attain their sincere harmony.

If we speak of the reach and influence of great music, at the culmination of joy and affectionate love, even Heaven and Earth will join in glad harmony—and how much more so superiors and inferiors? Yet without extending it to superiors and inferiors, there would be no way to see how profoundly the benefits of music are received. Therefore, the sage kings' bringing order and peace to the Chinese realm lay right within the strumming of strings and the beating of drums [? 緼㮣]. If we speak of the moving power [感乎, for 感孚] of supreme music, at the utmost of peace, harmony, and ease, even luxuriant vegetation rises up in universal compliance—and how much more so superiors and inferiors? Only by observing it between superiors and inferiors can one see how vast the responsive reach of music is. Therefore, the sage kings' calming and unifying of worldly contention was always manifested in the splendor of shields, battle-axes, feather-banners, and ox-tail pennants. Indeed, when the forms of music are shared in common, the transformative influence of non-contention is achieved; when superiors and inferiors are in harmony, all return to the blessing of being without resentment. Such is the way music remedies ritual.

論

聖世之民咸敦天秩而四海一心克奏協和之
化者何道哉以爲是下之所自致乎而下不能
===
自爲致也以爲是有術以驅之乎而要非術之
所能驅也煦睦雖爲自有之良然無所感而民
不動權智雖亦馭民之具然專用之而治愈煩
此其中固有不求於下不用乎法而天下自翕
然從治化其競絿亢戾之私而潛就於天親聚
順之美者則莫如先之以敬讓而民不爭之言
也斯言也子其得化民成俗之要乎請申其旨
粤稽唐虞三代之隆上之人本性情以昭示而
下之人亦本性情以訓行頑讒化而元凱登教
punctuated:
第貳場
論
「先之以敬讓而民不爭」　歐養淳

translation_en:
Second Session
Discourse
"Lead them with reverence and deference, and the people will not contend." — Ou Yangchun 歐養淳
Associate Examiner, Magistrate of Suiyang County, Zhang [read by Yuanke 元科]: Recommended.
Examiner, Secretary of the Capture Supervision Office under the Bureau of Operations in the Ministry of War, Xu [comment by Quan 銓]: Talent and thought burst forth swiftly.
Examiner, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites, Guo [comment by Maotai 茂泰]: Smooth and fluent.

By what Way is it that the people of a sage age all cultivate the heavenly order, and the Four Seas are of one mind, able to achieve the transformation of harmony and concord? Should we suppose that this is brought about by those below on their own? Yet those below cannot bring it about by themselves. Should we suppose that there are techniques to drive them to it? Yet in essence it is not something that techniques can drive them to do. Warmth and amity are indeed innate virtues, yet without something to move them, the people are not stirred; expedients and cleverness are indeed also tools for governing the people, yet if one relies exclusively on them, governance only grows more vexed. Herein there is truly a way that neither demands of those below nor relies on laws, whereby all under Heaven naturally and harmoniously follow good order, transforming their selfish impulses of contention, haste, arrogance, and perversity, and imperceptibly coming to the beauty of natural kinship and gathered compliance—nothing compares to the saying, "Lead them with reverence and deference, and the people will not contend." title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
化明而和平奏民風之淳莫淳於此矣民俗之
厚莫厚於此矣爭何有哉自黨庠術序之制廢
而民即於匪彝若是者則爭自愽典庸禮之化
弛而民失其天良若是者則爭自上之人不務
以身先天下不務以至情動兆人而所以日求
於下者惟苟且文具之爲而里黨無恪恭之意
鄉閭少謙遜之風若是者則爭是豈古民淳而
今民詐古俗厚而今俗薄與夫亦未端其本以
倡之也倡之維何亦先之以敬讓而已是故齋
===
藝允若上之自篤於一本者然也怡顏承志而
循循惟謹上之無忝於所生者然也推之而綱
常倫紀之間惟其情不惟其文言動事物之際
和於中國形於外兢兢之心抑抑之儀但爲一
身自盡之圖初非以爲感化羣倫之具然而民
之式型於下者其能自已乎試觀此日之民誰
有不敬誰敢不讓孝友任恤之情油然而動即
於匪彝者無有也恭讓端謹之習藹然而成失
其天良者無有也尊者安其爲尊卑者安其爲
punctuated: 化明而和平奏。民風之淳，莫淳於此矣；民俗之厚，莫厚於此矣，爭何有哉！自黨庠術序之制廢，而民即於匪彝，若是者則爭；自愽典庸禮之化弛，而民失其天良，若是者則爭；自上之人不務以身先天下，不務以至情動兆人，而所以日求於下者惟苟且文具之爲，而里黨無恪恭之意，鄉閭少謙遜之風，若是者則爭。是豈古民淳而今民詐，古俗厚而今俗薄與？夫亦未端其本以倡之也。倡之維何？亦先之以敬讓而已。是故齋藝允若，上之自篤於一本者然也；怡顏承志而循循惟謹，上之無忝於所生者然也。推之而綱常倫紀之間，惟其情不惟其文；言動事物之際，和於中固形於外。兢兢之心，抑抑之儀，但爲一身自盡之圖，初非以爲感化羣倫之具，然而民之式型於下者，其能自已乎？試觀此日之民，誰有不敬？誰敢不讓？孝友任恤之情油然而動，即於匪彝者無有也；恭讓端謹之習藹然而成，失其天良者無有也。尊者安其爲尊，卑者安其爲
translation_en: … instruction was clear, and peace and harmony were achieved. The purity of the people's ethos was never purer than this; the generosity of the people's customs was never more generous than this—what contention could there be! Ever since the system of local and district schools fell into disuse, the people have turned to deviance; when things are like this, there is contention. Ever since the transforming influence of upholding the constant norms and practicing the rites slackened, the people have lost their innate goodness; when things are like this, there is contention. Ever since those above ceased striving to lead the realm by personal example and ceased striving to move the multitude with utmost sincerity, seeking daily from those below only perfunctory formalities, neighborhood communities have lacked a spirit of respectful reverence, and rural villages have had little of the ethos of humble yielding; when things are like this, there is contention. Is it really that the people of antiquity were pure while the people of today are deceitful, or that the customs of antiquity were generous while the customs of today are shallow? It is simply that we have not rectified the root in order to lead them. And how does one lead them? Simply by going before them with reverence and yielding. Therefore, being solemn and reverent [?] and sincerely compliant—such is how those above devote themselves to their single root; maintaining a pleasant countenance to carry out their parents' wishes, following in an orderly and cautious manner—such is how those above bring no disgrace to those who gave them life. Extending this to the realm of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues, they care for genuine feeling and not mere outward form; in matters of speech, conduct, and daily affairs, harmony within certainly manifests without. A cautious heart and a restrained demeanor are meant only as a way to fulfill one's own personal duty, not originally as instruments for transforming the multitude—and yet how could the people below stop themselves from taking them as their model? Just look at the people of such a day: who would not be reverent? Who would dare not yield? Feelings of filial piety, brotherly love, mutual trust, and compassion arise spontaneously, and there is no one who turns to deviance; habits of respectful yielding and upright caution take shape amicably, and there is no one who loses their innate goodness. Those of noble station are content in being noble, and those of humble station are content in being…

punctuated: 表稱謝者。伏以武功茂著，遐方仰天子之威；文德誕敷，絕域沐聖人之化。靖烽煙於萬里，萬年之兵氣長消；闢土宇於一方，一統之輿圖永廓。榮生符竹，慶溢海澨。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟聖王奠鼎，萃九州玉帛之隆；哲后齊圖，擴四海車書之盛。舞虞階之干羽，德被苗民；集商室之共球，威揚下國。江漢肅清於姬代，《徹土》美式闢之休；淮海底定於魯邦，《獻琛》頌集泮之盛。漢平交趾，馬伏波之銅柱稱雄；唐靖淮蔡，韓昌黎之檄書誌異。然尚遡漢文之奉贄，亦旣盛矣，而南粵、旣閩未入版圖；迨考夫建元之黷武，伊云烈哉，而邛、筰、珠崖僅歸宇內。載稽宋代，非不
translation_en:
… a memorial to express our gratitude.

We humbly reflect that as martial achievements brilliantly manifest, distant quarters look up to the majesty of the Son of Heaven; as civil virtue broadly extends, remote realms bathe in the transforming influence of the Sage. Quelling the beacon-fires across ten thousand li, the aura of weaponry is forever dispelled for ten thousand years; opening up territory in a whole region, the map of unified rule is permanently expanded. Glory springs from the tallies and bamboo credentials of office, and celebration overflows to the shores of the sea. In utmost fear and trepidation, bowing our heads to the ground, your servants submit these words:

We humbly observe that when the sage kings of old established their tripods of sovereignty, they gathered the flourishing tribute of jade and silk from all the Nine Provinces; when wise sovereigns ordered their realms, they expanded the grand uniformity of axle-widths and script across the Four Seas. When shields and feathers were danced on the steps of Yu [Shun], virtue reached the Miao people; when tributary jade emblems were assembled in the house of Shang, majesty was proclaimed throughout the vassal states. When the Yangzi and Han river regions were pacified in the Zhou dynasty, the ode "Tithe the Land" [Classic of Poetry, "Jiang Han"] praised the blessing of expanding the realm; when the Huai River and the sea were settled for the state of Lu, the verse "Presenting Treasures" [Classic of Poetry, "Pan Shui"] lauded the splendor of gathering at the semicircular water of the state school. When the Han pacified Jiaozhi, the bronze pillars of Ma the Wave-Subduing General (Ma Yuan 馬援) were hailed for their heroism; when the Tang quieted Huai and Cai, the proclamation written by Han Changli (Han Yu 韓愈) recorded the extraordinary feat. Yet if we trace back to the presentation of tributary gifts under Emperor Wen of Han, though it was already flourishing, Southern Yue and Min [?] had not yet entered the imperial registers; and when we examine the militarism of the Jianyuan reign (140–135 BCE) under Emperor Wu of Han, fierce as it was said to be, Qiong, Zuo, and Zhuya were merely brought within the realm. Further examining the Song dynasty, it was not that they did not …

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
慕王會之圖遞及明初亦徒假一統之志
未有開疆拓地
震疊暨於遐陬分職設官
風猷振於薄海如
今日者也茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
允文允武
作君作師
赫聲濯靈化徧無雷之國
===
宣威布德光騰出日之鄉奕奕寰區六宇盡
屬職方之掌茫茫續甸四海悉是疆索之
編三逆既平已知山無伏莽一隅向化尤
見海不揚波維彼臺灣連乎閩省從前挾
飛舸以蕩搖幾等鯨鯢之出沒今此望鐵
騎而輸款不復烽燧之縱橫捷書遙傳已
識
天顏有喜凱歌聿奏爾覺
帝德無疆爰置郡縣之名用設官僚之職城垣
punctuated: 慕《王會》之圖，遞及明初，亦徒假一統之志。未有開疆拓地，震疊暨於遐陬，分職設官，風猷振於薄海，如今日者也。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下允文允武，作君作師。赫聲濯靈，化徧無雷之國；宣威布德，光騰出日之鄉。奕奕寰區，六宇盡屬職方之掌；茫茫續甸，四海悉是疆索之編。三逆既平，已知山無伏莽；一隅向化，尤見海不揚波。維彼臺灣，連乎閩省，從前挾飛舸以蕩搖，幾等鯨鯢之出沒；今此望鐵騎而輸款，不復烽燧之縱橫。捷書遙傳，已識天顏有喜；凱歌聿奏，爾覺帝德無疆。爰置郡縣之名，用設官僚之職。城垣
translation_en:
…covet the illustrations of the Royal Audience (Wanghui), and passing down to the early Ming, they likewise merely laid false claim to the ambition of grand unification. Never before have borders been opened and lands expanded so that awe and trembling reached the farthest corners, or duties apportioned and officials established so that wind-like influence and grand plans stirred up to the very edges of the seas, as they do today.

This is because we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, truly civil and truly martial, acting as sovereign and acting as teacher. With glorious renown and resplendent majesty, Your transforming influence pervades the lands of Wulei; manifesting prestige and spreading virtue, Your radiance soars over the regions of the rising sun. Across the grand terrestrial realm, the six directions all belong under the charge of the Bureau of Operations (Zhifang); throughout the vast and continuous imperial domain, the four seas are entirely enrolled within the registers of our territories. Since the Three Feudatories were pacified, it is already known that the mountains harbor no hidden bandits; and as this single corner turns toward civilization, it is especially evident that the seas do not raise their waves.

Now that Taiwan is linked to the province of Fujian; formerly they relied on swift galleys to toss and unsettle, almost like whales andleviathans emerging and vanishing; now they gaze upon our iron cavalry and tender their submission, so that beacon fires no longer crisscross the land. As dispatches of victory are transmitted from afar, we already know that the Heavenly Countenance rejoices; as songs of triumph are performed, we feel all the more [?] that the Imperial Virtue is boundless. Thereupon the designations of prefectures and counties have been instituted, and the offices of bureaucrats and magistrates established. City walls…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
初築添禹貢之所未詳符綏新增廣周官
之所未備爲錢穀爲刑名治遠無殊於治
近或兵農或禮樂外安益致夫內安將見
被良有司之撫循總屬沐
聖天子之德化拓其地者卽有以定其地永列
星羅碁布之中臣其人者卽有以安其人
益堅服教畏神之戴卓哉
皇威之遠播允矣
聖澤之遐周臣等才慚投筆識愧借籌幸際
===
昌時正値海晏河清之會欣逢
盛世適遘民安物阜之休聽海氛旣平歡同
獸舞覩花縣初置喜溢雀騰瞻五色之
絲綸仰
一人之浩蕩伏願
柔遠能邇
養民致賢
修文偃武風清禹服五千
布愷行慈德沛商圍九有則金甌永固治登
punctuated: 初築，添《禹貢》之所未詳；符綏新增，廣《周官》之所未備。爲錢穀，爲刑名，治遠無殊於治近；或兵農，或禮樂，外安益致夫內安。將見被良有司之撫循，總屬沐聖天子之德化。拓其地者，卽有以定其地，永列星羅碁布之中；臣其人者，卽有以安其人，益堅服教畏神之戴。卓哉皇威之遠播，允矣聖澤之遐周！臣等才慚投筆，識愧借籌。幸際昌時，正値海晏河清之會；欣逢盛世，適遘民安物阜之休。聽海氛旣平，歡同獸舞；覩花縣初置，喜溢雀騰。瞻五色之絲綸，仰一人之浩蕩。伏願柔遠能邇，養民致賢。修文偃武，風清禹服五千；布愷行慈，德沛商圍九有。則金甌永固，治登
translation_en: …are newly built, adding what was not detailed in the Tribute of Yu (Yugong); tallies and seal-cords are newly increased, expanding upon what was not provided for in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). Whether in fiscal administration or in judicial affairs, governing the distant is no different from governing the near; whether in military and agricultural matters or in rites and music, peace on the frontier further brings about peace within the realm. It shall soon be seen that receiving the soothing guidance of capable local officials is altogether a matter of being bathed in the moral transformation of the Sacred Son of Heaven. Having expanded into this territory, there are forthwith the means to stabilize this territory, placing it forever amid the prefectures and counties arrayed like stars and chess pieces; having made subjects of its people, there are forthwith the means to pacify its people, making ever firmer their allegiance in submitting to instruction and standing in awe of divine majesty. Illustrious indeed is the far-flung reach of Imperial awe; truly boundless is the distant encompassment of Sacred beneficence! Your servants are ashamed of our lack of talent to cast aside the writing brush for military service, and humbled by our lack of foresight to lend strategic counsel. Fortunately encountering a prosperous era, we meet with this juncture of calm seas and clear rivers; joyfully witnessing a flourishing age, we happen upon the blessings of a peaceful populace and abundant resources. Hearing that the maritime miasma has been quelled, we rejoice like the dancing beasts of yore; beholding the flower-like counties newly established, we overflow with the delight of leaping sparrows. Gazing upon the five-colored silken edicts, we look up to the vast bounty of the One Man. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will cherish the distant and be gracious to the near, nourish the people and attract the worthy; cultivate civil virtue and lay down weapons, so that pure winds sweep through the five thousand li of Yu's domains; spread kindness and practice compassion, so that virtue floods the nine regions of Shang's realm. Then the golden vessel of the empire shall be forever secure, governance shall ascend above…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
六五四三而玉燭長調祚衍百千萬億矣
臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
===
第一問
王廷梅
同考試官德陽縣知縣許〔震元閱　薦〕
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事凃〔銓批　簡要〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批　清和〕
帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心心與
道合而治法昭焉蓋不可或斁者基命宥
密之微而不可不討者經國久遠之務此
唐虞三代盛時君臣誥誡致謹一心所以
punctuated:
六五四三，而玉燭長調，祚衍百千萬億矣。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第一問。
王廷梅。
同考試官德陽縣知縣許〔震元閱　薦〕。
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事凃〔銓批　簡要〕。
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批　清和〕。

帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心，心與道合而治法昭焉。蓋不可或斁者，基命宥密之微；而不可不討者，經國久遠之務。此唐虞三代盛時，君臣誥誡，致謹一心，所以
translation_en:
… the Six Honored Ones, Five Emperors, Four Seasons, and Three Dynasties [?], and the Jade Candle of cosmic harmony will forever keep the seasons in balance, extending the dynastic fortune for hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds of millions of years. Your servants, looking up toward Heaven and gazing upon Your Sacred Majesty, are overwhelmed with earnest emotion and awe-struck trepidation, and respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for the Imperial hearing.

Third Session: Five Policy Questions.

First Question.
By Wang Tingmei 王廷梅.
Associate Examiner Xu Zhenuan 許震元, District Magistrate of Deyang District [read and recommended].
Examiner Tu Quan 凃銓, Secretary for Apprehension in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War [comment: Concise and essential].

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
治臻慼隆〻而成雍和之風爲漢唐宋之所
莫及者豈非以心法爲道法之本而仰道
法爲治法之要乎我
皇上英敏性成亶聰建極四海之內皆已乂安
綱紀之群悉已允釐禮樂文章之被悉已
遐訖則一代之治法與道法洵可以媲美
唐虞三代而無媿者也而
執事以心法下詢復計及於久安長治斯誠
効忠之至意乎愚生請敬陳之從來君臨
===
天下者類必有勵精圖治之心而後可以
建百代之烈亦必有慎始謀終之志而始
能以裕萬世之猷故雖道法所以爲作則
之矩而治法所以爲蕩平之畧然其要惟
自人君之一心基之葢君心爲宰制之原
萬方之憂樂係焉使少有不毖則怠忽乘
之其能望道法之克昭而爲治法之永垂
也哉考之隆古其道法之被於史册而萬
世仰治平之績者昭若日星欲一則曰儆
punctuated: 治臻慼隆〻而成雍和之風，爲漢、唐、宋之所莫及者，豈非以心法爲道法之本，而仰道法爲治法之要乎？我皇上英敏性成，亶聰建極，四海之內皆已乂安，綱紀之群悉已允釐，禮樂文章之被悉已遐訖，則一代之治法與道法，洵可以媲美唐、虞、三代而無媿者也。而執事以心法下詢，復計及於久安長治，斯誠効忠之至意乎！愚生請敬陳之。從來君臨天下者，類必有勵精圖治之心，而後可以建百代之烈；亦必有慎始謀終之志，而始能以裕萬世之猷。故雖道法所以爲作則之矩，而治法所以爲蕩平之畧，然其要惟自人君之一心基之。葢君心爲宰制之原，萬方之憂樂係焉。使少有不毖，則怠忽乘之，其能望道法之克昭，而爲治法之永垂也哉？考之隆古，其道法之被於史册，而萬世仰治平之績者，昭若日星。欲一則曰「儆…
translation_en:
…governance reached flourishing prosperity [?] and formed an ethos of harmony and concord that the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties could not match—was it not because they took the method of the mind as the root of the method of the Way, and looked to the method of the Way as the essential of the method of governance?

Our August Emperor is naturally endowed with heroic acuity, possessing genuine sagely intelligence and establishing the supreme standard. Within the four seas all is already in tranquil order; the array of fundamental laws and institutions is altogether regulated and rectified; and the reach of rites, music, and cultural refinement has extended to the farthest regions. Thus, the method of governance and the method of the Way in our own era can truly rival the beauty of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties without shame. Yet Your Excellency condescends to inquire about the method of the mind, taking further account of enduring peace and lasting order—is this not truly the utmost intention of rendering loyal service? I, a humble student, beg to respectfully set this forth.

From of old, those who reign as sovereign over All under Heaven have generally had to possess a mind roused to vigor in seeking good governance before they could establish achievements for a hundred generations; they have also had to possess the resolve to be cautious at the beginning and plan for the end before they could enrich counsels for ten thousand generations. Therefore, although the method of the Way is the standard by which rules are made, and the method of governance is the strategy by which broad and level order is achieved, their essential point is founded solely upon the single mind of the ruler. For the ruler's mind is the source of sovereign control, upon which the sorrows and joys of the myriad regions depend. If there is the slightest lack of caution, laxity and negligence will take advantage of it; how then could one hope for the method of the Way to be made illustrious and the method of governance to be handed down forever?

Examining high antiquity, how the method of the Way was recorded in the historical annals, and how ten thousand generations looked up to their achievements of order and peace, shines as brightly as the sun and stars. Yet [?] in one instance it is said, "Be admonished…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
戒無虞一則曰勅天之命惟時惟幾以至
周公之告成王曰君子所其無逸非皆以
古聖之心法為道法所從出而一代之治
法本諸道法而盡善乎我
國家昇平永久而治法與道法交勵於
宸衷之乾惕者罔有或斁固已駕軼漢唐宋而
追踪盛古者也然為萬年計有道之長惟
在謹始圖終單心夙夜而已於以上幾郅
隆持盈保泰端在斯乎
===
第二問
高之霖
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閱〕薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批〕清通
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批〕明湛
一代之風俗一代之德教為之也德之未
至則身範不端何以統六宇而歸化教之
不早則規制未立又何以範九有而從風
無惑乎其厭樸而喜華好奢而惡嗇也惟
punctuated:
戒無虞」，一則曰「勅天之命，惟時惟幾」，以至周公之告成王曰「君子所其無逸」，非皆以古聖之心法為道法所從出，而一代之治法本諸道法而盡善乎？我國家昇平永久，而治法與道法交勵於宸衷之乾惕者，罔有或斁，固已駕軼漢、唐、宋而追踪盛古者也。然為萬年計有道之長，惟在謹始圖終，單心夙夜而已。於以上幾郅隆，持盈保泰，端在斯乎！

第二問
高之霖
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閱〕薦
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批〕清通
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批〕明湛

一代之風俗，一代之德教為之也。德之未至，則身範不端，何以統六宇而歸化？教之不早，則規制未立，又何以範九有而從風？無惑乎其厭樸而喜華、好奢而惡嗇也！惟…
translation_en:
… against the unforeseen,” and in another says, “Respectfully obey the Mandate of Heaven, at every moment and in every subtle incipient sign,” down to the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) admonishing King Cheng (Cheng Wang 成王), saying, “The noble man makes freedom from idleness his dwelling place”—do not all of these take the method of the mind-and-heart of the ancient sages as the source from which the principles of the Way issue forth, so that the methods of governance of an era are rooted in those principles of the Way and thus reach perfection? Our Dynasty enjoys enduring peace and prosperity, and the way in which methods of governance and principles of the Way mutually reinforce one another through the tireless vigilance of the Imperial mind has never known weariness; indeed, it has already surpassed the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties and followed in the footsteps of flourishing antiquity. Yet, in planning for the longevity of righteous rule over ten thousand years, it lies solely in being cautious at the beginning and mindful of the end, devoting the whole heart from morning till night. By this means to ascend toward supreme prosperity, maintaining fullness and preserving peace—does it not rest squarely upon this!

Second Question
By Gao Zhilin 高之霖.
Associate Examiner Zhang Yuanke 章元科, District Magistrate of Suiyang County 綏陽縣, read and recommended.
Examiner Tu Quan 涂銓, Secretary of the Bureau of Operations in the Ministry of War (supervising the capture of fugitives), commented: “Lucid and coherent.”
Examiner Guo Maotai 郭茂泰, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites, commented: “Clear and profound.”

The customs of an age are shaped by the moral instruction of that age. If virtue has not reached its perfection, then personal example is not upright—how then can one unite the six directions and bring them to transformation? If instruction is not given early, then regulations and institutions are not established—how then can one mold the nine regions so that they follow the wind of influence? It is no wonder that people despise simplicity and delight in华丽 extravagance, loving luxury and hating frugality! Only…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
有以轉移而化導之則後靡不作致一世
於淳厚之休而無難我
皇上酌文質之中定制宜民而又崇尚節儉以
爲天下先且有司奉行巳久宜其化行俗
美矣而
執事猶以浮靡僭侈爲慮愚試言其所見可
乎竊以爲
朝廷之倡率不貴有其文而貴有其實則巳節
巳儉尤當求其無不節無不儉也有司之
===
奉行不徒有其法而務有其誠則奉行之
既力尤當勉其無不力也民其因是而知
所觀感乎而猶有進焉者一則孝弟力田
之科不可不設也出也負耒入也横經則
恒心與恒產而俱全矣一則陳詩納賈之
制不可不舉也司徒章教太史採風則歌
叙得勸戒而可久矣一則節性防淫之典
不可不行也食必以時用必有禮則性情
因制防而不乖矣且也辨上下之分定隆
punctuated: 有以轉移而化導之，則後靡不作，致一世於淳厚之休而無難。我皇上酌文質之中，定制宜民，而又崇尚節儉，以爲天下先，且有司奉行巳久，宜其化行俗美矣。而執事猶以浮靡僭侈爲慮，愚試言其所見可乎？竊以爲朝廷之倡率，不貴有其文，而貴有其實，則巳節巳儉，尤當求其無不節、無不儉也；有司之奉行，不徒有其法，而務有其誠，則奉行之既力，尤當勉其無不力也。民其因是而知所觀感乎！而猶有進焉者：一則孝弟力田之科不可不設也，出也負耒，入也横經，則恒心與恒產而俱全矣；一則陳詩納賈之制不可不舉也，司徒章教，太史採風，則歌叙得勸戒而可久矣；一則節性防淫之典不可不行也，食必以時，用必有禮，則性情因制防而不乖矣。且也辨上下之分，定隆
translation_en:
… one has the means to transform and guide them through moral instruction, then extravagance [reading 後 as 侈] will not arise, and there will be no difficulty in bringing the entire age to the blessing of pure and generous customs. Our Emperor weighs the balance between refinement and substance, establishes regulations suited to the people, and furthermore esteems frugality so as to set an example for all under Heaven. Moreover, the authorities have long been carrying out these policies, so it ought to be that moral transformation prevails and customs are admirable. Yet Your Excellency is still concerned about superficiality, extravagance, and presumptuous luxury. May this humble candidate attempt to state his views?

I venture to think that in leading by example, the court should value not the mere outward form, but the reality: where it is already frugal and thrifty, it ought still more to seek that there be nothing in which it is not frugal and nothing in which it is not thrifty. In carrying out orders, the authorities should not merely possess the regulations, but strive to possess sincerity: where their implementation is already vigorous, they ought still more to exert themselves so that there is nothing in which they are not vigorous. Would the people not thereby know what to look up to and be moved by?

And yet there is still more to be advanced: First, the recruitment category of the filial, fraternal, and diligent in farming (xiaoti litian) must be established. When going out they carry the plow on their shoulders, and when coming in they lay the classics across their knees; thus both constant minds and constant livelihoods will be complete. Second, the institution of presenting folk odes and reporting market prices must be revived. When the Minister of Education (situ) illustrates moral instruction and the Grand Scribe (taishi) collects the airs of the states, songs and narratives will attain encouragement and admonition and can endure for long. Third, the statutes for regulating human nature and preventing licentiousness must be put into practice. When food is consumed strictly according to season and expenditures are made strictly according to ritual propriety, then human dispositions and emotions will not go awry because of regulatory bounds. Furthermore, one should distinguish the ranks of superior and inferior, fix the proper degrees of abundance and…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
殺之宜範一代以大中至正之軌使天下
之人秀者愚者皆凜凜然就於天叙天秩
之經而不可越則浮靡之習日以消矣浮
靡消而有不儉者乎則僭侈之心漸以化
矣僭侈化而有不厚者乎風俗成於斯人
心正於斯其斯爲轉移化導之要歟蒭蕘
之言亦有當於
執事之問否
第三問
===
歐養淳
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閲　薦〕
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批　剴切〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批　周到〕
將以正天下而法可盡廢乎廢乎法則善
者無以自安而不善者返獲保全之慶將
以仁天下而法可盡恃乎恃乎法則君子
有懷刑之懼而小人終無以爲自新之階
所以古來聖王本夫不得不用之心而嘗
punctuated:
殺之宜，範一代以大中至正之軌，使天下之人，秀者、愚者皆凜凜然就於天叙天秩之經而不可越。則浮靡之習日以消矣，浮靡消而有不儉者乎？則僭侈之心漸以化矣，僭侈化而有不厚者乎？風俗成於斯，人心正於斯，其斯爲轉移化導之要歟！蒭蕘之言，亦有當於執事之問否？

第三問
歐養淳
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閲　薦〕
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批　剴切〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批　周到〕

將以正天下而法可盡廢乎？廢乎法則善者無以自安，而不善者返獲保全之慶。將以仁天下而法可盡恃乎？恃乎法則君子有懷刑之懼，而小人終無以爲自新之階。所以古來聖王，本夫不得不用之心，而嘗
translation_en:
… the propriety of elaboration and curtailment, and mold a generation within the tracks of supreme impartiality and utmost rectitude, causing all people in the realm, whether refined or simple, to reverently conform to the constant principles of the Heaven-ordained social order and ritual hierarchy without daring to transgress them. Then habits of frivolity and extravagance will daily diminish; when frivolity and extravagance diminish, could anyone fail to be frugal? Then minds given to僭usurpation and luxury will gradually be transformed; when usurpation and luxury are transformed, could anyone fail to be generous and sincere? Customs are perfected through this, and human hearts are rectified through this—is this not the essential key to transforming and guiding the people! May these humble words of a grass-and-firewood gatherer perhaps prove fitting as a response to Your Excellency's question?

Question Three
Ou Yangchun 歐養淳
Associate Examiner Zhang Yuan 章元, Magistrate of Suiyang County 〔read by genres/subject [科閲] — recommended〕
Examiner Tu Quan 涂銓, Secretary for Arrests in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War 〔comment: incisive and pertinent〕
Examiner Guo Maotai 郭茂泰, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies of the Ministry of Rites 〔comment: thorough and comprehensive〕

In seeking to rectify the realm, can laws be entirely abolished? If laws are abolished, the good have no means to rest secure in themselves, while the wicked instead reap the fortune of self-preservation. In seeking to govern the realm with benevolence, can laws be entirely relied upon? If laws are relied upon alone, the superior man harbors the dread of punishment, while the petty man ultimately has no stepping-stone by which to renew himself. Therefore, the sage kings of antiquity, acting from a heart that resorted to punishments only out of necessity, always…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
獄成之時眞僞互竄其隱心出於恕與淸
則惟官惟貨之類皆不足以惑志氣而亂
獄辭此所謂以欽恤之情行寬大之法者
也古帝王所以幾刑措者率此道也今誠
能由此道以致治則於楊之下皆爲仁人
之樂愷鞭笞之間無非長者之藹吉愚生
請以成中之慶無疆之辭爲我
國家頌焉
第四問
===
歐養淳
同考試官綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閱　薦〕
考試官兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批　具見經術〕
考試官禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批　洞悉時勢〕
執事籌畫餉之道而議及於屯政謂蜀中之
大務自生聚而外莫有急於此者也夫守
其土卽食其土之所有於民無轉餽之勞
於兵受飽騰之益甚便利也而未之舉行
者豈不以攻取之時不遑議及承平之日
punctuated:
獄成之時，眞僞互竄，其隱心出於恕與淸，則惟官、惟貨之類，皆不足以惑志氣而亂獄辭，此所謂以欽恤之情，行寬大之法者也。古帝王所以幾刑措者，率此道也。今誠能由此道以致治，則於楊之下，皆爲仁人之樂愷；鞭笞之間，無非長者之藹吉。愚生請以成中之慶、無疆之辭，爲我國家頌焉。

第四問

歐養淳
同考試官、綏陽縣知縣章〔元科閱　薦〕
考試官、兵部職方司督捕主事涂〔銓批　具見經術〕
考試官、禮部儀制司郎中郭〔茂泰批　洞悉時勢〕

執事籌畫餉之道，而議及於屯政，謂蜀中之大務，自生聚而外，莫有急於此者也。夫守其土，卽食其土之所有，於民無轉餽之勞，於兵受飽騰之益，甚便利也。而未之舉行者，豈不以攻取之時，不遑議及，承平之日，
translation_en:
…At the time when a case is concluded, truth and falsehood become intertwined and altered; yet if one's innermost heart proceeds from empathy and purity, then influences such as official favoritism or bribery will all be insufficient to confuse one's resolve and spirit or tothrow the legal depositions into disorder. This is what is meant by carrying out magnanimous laws with a sentiment of reverent compassion. The means by which the ancient emperors and kings nearly brought about the setting aside of punishments altogether followed this very way. If today we can truly follow this way to achieve good governance, then beneath the cangue [reading 楊 as 桁] all will experience the joyful kindness of benevolent men, and amidst the use of the whip and rod there will be nothing but the gentle auspiciousness of virtuous elders. Your humble student begs to offer the felicity of "attaining the mean" and the words of "boundless" [blessing, from the Book of Documents] in praise of our Dynasty.

Fourth Question

Ou Yangchun 歐養淳.
Associate Examiner, Magistrate of Suiyang County, Zhang [Yuanke 章元科 read and recommended].
Examiner, Secretary in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War Assigned to Supervise the Capture of Fugitives, Tu [Quan 涂銓 commented: Fully demonstrates statecraft grounded in the Classics].
Examiner, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites, Guo [Maotai 郭茂泰 commented: Thoroughly understands the current situation].

Your Excellency plans the way of provisioning military rations and extends the discussion to the administration of military state farms (tunzheng), stating that among the great affairs of Sichuan (Shu), apart from fostering population growth and accumulating resources, nothing is more urgent than this. Now, for those who garrison a territory to feed directly upon what that territory produces spares the common people the toil of transporting supplies and grants the soldiers the benefit of being well-fed and vigorous—it is exceedingly advantageous. Yet why has this not been put into practice? Is it not because in times of conquest and seizure there was no leisure to deliberate upon it, while in days of peace…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
患非有預備之策何以爲善後之圖哉我
皇上軫念蜀省
詔旨屢頒懸招民之賞格寬起科之年限免續
墾勸墾之田糧所以爲蜀民計者至深且
遠然而載在版籍者不敵他省之一郡戶
口之凋殘如故也沃野千里古有其稱而
今一望榛莽田疇之未闢如故也城市之
間半爲瓦礫而往來道途者落落晨星井
里之丘墟如故也是則不患無可耕之田
===
而患無可耕之人不患耕耘之不致其力
而患生聚之無其法力穡備荒之術不綦
難哉然亦無難也蓋他省之民當思所以
招徠之賞格久懸而人無有應者則以數
多而力有不給也何若變通成例厚其賞
而減其數則應之者踵相接也流移之衆
當思所以安集之人情誰不回首鄉井若
於資斧之無具耳何若官給以糗糧舟車
之費計其多寡以爲鼓勵則急公者亦不
punctuated: 患？非有預備之策，何以爲善後之圖哉？我皇上軫念蜀省，詔旨屢頒，懸招民之賞格，寬起科之年限，免續墾、勸墾之田糧，所以爲蜀民計者至深且遠。然而載在版籍者不敵他省之一郡，戶口之凋殘如故也；沃野千里，古有其稱，而今一望榛莽，田疇之未闢如故也；城市之間半爲瓦礫，而往來道途者落落晨星，井里之丘墟如故也。是則不患無可耕之田，而患無可耕之人；不患耕耘之不致其力，而患生聚之無其法。力穡備荒之術，不綦難哉？然亦無難也。蓋他省之民，當思所以招徠之。賞格久懸而人無有應者，則以數多而力有不給也。何若變通成例，厚其賞而減其數，則應之者踵相接也。流移之衆，當思所以安集之。人情誰不回首鄉井？若於資斧之無具耳。何若官給以糗糧、舟車之費，計其多寡以爲鼓勵，則急公者亦不
translation_en: … calamity? Without preparatory measures, how can we plan for rehabilitation? Our Emperor feels deep concern for Sichuan province, and imperial decrees have been repeatedly issued: establishing reward scales for recruiting settlers, extending the grace period before land taxes are levied, and granting exemptions from grain taxes on newly reclaimed and encouraged-reclamation lands. His plans on behalf of the people of Sichuan are thus utmost in their depth and reach. And yet, those recorded in the household registers do not equal even a single prefecture of another province—the decimation of the population remains as before. In antiquity this land was famed as a thousand li of fertile plains, yet today one gazes out upon brambles and weeds—the uncultivated state of the fields remains as before. Half of the cities and towns lie in rubble, and travelers along the roads are as sparse as morning stars—the ruin of the villages and wards remains as before. Thus, the worry is not that there are no fields fit for tilling, but that there are no people to till them; the worry is not that people fail to exert their strength in plowing and weeding, but that there is no method for fostering population growth and gathering communities. Is not the art of diligent farming and preparing against famine exceedingly difficult? Yet it is not difficult after all. Regarding the people of other provinces, we ought to consider how to attract them. That the scale of rewards has long been posted without anyone responding is because the required quotas of settlers are too high and people's means are insufficient to meet them. Why not flexibly adapt the established regulations, increasing the rewards while reducing the required numbers? Then those responding will follow closely on one another's heels. Regarding the displaced multitudes, we ought to consider how to settle and gather them. Given human nature, who does not look back with longing toward their native village? They are merely distressed [reading 苦 for 若] by the lack of travel funds and provisions. Why not have the authorities supply them with dry provisions and the costs of boats and carts, calculating the numbers brought back as a basis for encouragement and reward? Then those eager to serve the public good will likewise not…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
甘於自後矣如是有可耕之人而復爲之
給其牛種之具善其撫綏之謀則無無不耕
之田亦無不備之荒矣敢以是上紓
聖天子西顧之慮焉
punctuated: 甘於自後矣。如是有可耕之人，而復爲之給其牛種之具，善其撫綏之謀，則無無不耕之田，亦無不備之荒矣。敢以是上紓聖天子西顧之慮焉。
translation_en: …willing to lag behind. In this way, once there are people able to till the land, and we further provide them with oxen and seed and perfect the plans for their pacification and comfort, there will be no fields left uncultivated [?] and no famine unprepared for. I venture to offer this on high to relieve the Sacred Son of Heaven's anxious concern for the West.

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄後序
歲甲子天下復當較士於鄉
四川之役
皇上命臣銓副禮曹郎臣茂秦往
典厥事伏念臣三楚豎儒學
術弇淺蒙
恩由外吏拔擢辦事樞曹恆兢兢
===
隕越是懼茲復恭膺
簡命得與持衡重任益恐掄選無
當負
皇上旁求至意懼滋甚然殫智畢
慮黽勉將事以仰答
先命臣不敢以懼自阻也爰戴星
浥露叱馭而前度雲棧之險
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄後序

歲甲子，天下復當較士於鄉。四川之役，皇上命臣銓副禮曹郎臣茂秦往典厥事。伏念臣三楚豎儒，學術弇淺，蒙恩由外吏拔擢，辦事樞曹，恆兢兢隕越是懼。茲復恭膺簡命，得與持衡重任，益恐掄選無當，負皇上旁求至意，懼滋甚。然殫智畢慮，黽勉將事，以仰答先命，臣不敢以懼自阻也。爰戴星浥露，叱馭而前，度雲棧之險，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the jiazi year (1684), the realm was once again due to examine scholars in the provinces. For the mission to Sichuan, His Majesty commanded Your Servant Quan to serve as deputy to Your Servant Maoqin, Secretary in the Ministry of Rites, to go and preside over the affair. I humbly reflect that I am a mere petty scholar from the Three Chu region, shallow and narrow in learning. Having received imperial grace in being promoted from a provincial post to handle affairs in the Ministry of War, I have constantly been in trembling fear of failing in my duties. Now, having respectfully received this selective commission and been permitted to share in the weighty responsibility of holding the scales of evaluation, I fear all the more that my selection of talents may be inappropriate and fail to live up to His Majesty's utmost intention of seeking out men of ability from all quarters; thus my fear grows even greater. Yet to exhaust my wisdom and thoughts and strive diligently in carrying out this task so as to respectfully answer the Sovereign's mandate [? 先命, likely a transcription error for 寵命 or 成命]—I dare not let fear hold me back. Accordingly, traveling under the stars and wet with dew, I urged my carriage forward, crossing the perilous plank roads in the clouds,…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
歷蜀道之難計程疾馳幸如
期而至止焉比抵闈朝夕恪
恭與正考分考諸臣矢公矢
慎以襄乃事事竣臣茂泰既
颺言簡端矣臣例應再賡篇
末因伏思我
國家登進賢才首重制科誠欲
於書升論秀之中拔其尤儲
其才以備疏附後先之任使
用成師師濟濟之休是今日
賢書之所登即他年公卿大
夫之布列也士之懷才待試
思得一當以見售於時者亦
非僅爲一身之榮將出其素
punctuated: 歷蜀道之難，計程疾馳，幸如期而至止焉。比抵闈，朝夕恪恭，與正考、分考諸臣矢公矢慎，以襄乃事。事竣，臣茂泰既颺言簡端矣，臣例應再賡篇末。因伏思我國家登進賢才，首重制科，誠欲於書升論秀之中，拔其尤、儲其才，以備疏附後先之任使，用成師師濟濟之休。是今日賢書之所登，即他年公卿大夫之布列也。士之懷才待試，思得一當以見售於時者，亦非僅爲一身之榮，將出其素
translation_en:
…and passing through the hardships of the Road to Shu, I calculated the stages and galloped swiftly, fortunate enough to arrive on schedule. Once I reached the examination compound, morning and evening I maintained reverent diligence, swearing an oath of impartiality and caution together with the Chief Examiner and the Associate Examiners so as to bring this matter to completion. Now that the task is concluded, Your Servant [Fang] Maotai 方茂泰 has already set forth his words at the head of the volume, and by precedent Your Servant ought to contribute a sequel at the end of the text.

Thereupon I humbly reflect that in promoting worthy talents, our dynasty places foremost weight upon the regular civil examinations. Truly its aim is, in the course of registering and evaluating the finest scholars, to select the most outstanding and store up their talent, so as to prepare them for employment as ministers who draw the distant near and who lead and follow, thereby achieving the splendid harmony of an abundance of mutually emulating officials. Thus those who are entered today in the register of the worthy are none other than those who in future years will fill the ranks of the high ministers and grandees. As for scholars who cherish talent and await examination, hoping to meet with an opportunity to win recognition in their time, this too is not merely for the glory of their own persons; they are about to bring forth what they have ordinarily…

title: 康熙二十三年四川鄉試錄
text:
所蓄積表見於天下也古大
儒修之於家獻之於廷經術
有本處則爲醇儒經世致用
出則爲名臣文章經濟二者
合而致之非判然兩途也惟
平日有眞學問斯發爲文章
如日月之明金石之聲江海
===
之濤瀾虎豹之炳蔚起弊扶
衰而一代之文運賴以振興
亦惟有眞學問斯出爲經濟
上可以黼藻昇平下可以霖
雨兆姓樹鴻勳於永世紀成
績於太常宣猷展釆而一代
之事功因之日起如是則取
punctuated: 所蓄積表見於天下也。古大儒修之於家，獻之於廷；經術有本，處則爲醇儒；經世致用，出則爲名臣。文章、經濟二者合而致之，非判然兩途也。惟平日有眞學問，斯發爲文章，如日月之明、金石之聲、江海之濤瀾、虎豹之炳蔚，起弊扶衰，而一代之文運賴以振興；亦惟有眞學問，斯出爲經濟，上可以黼藻昇平，下可以霖雨兆姓，樹鴻勳於永世，紀成績於太常，宣猷展釆，而一代之事功因之日起。如是，則取
translation_en: …they have long accumulated, so as to manifest it before All Under Heaven. The great Confucian scholars of antiquity cultivated themselves at home and offered their service at court. With classical learning firmly rooted, in retirement they were pure Confucian scholars; ordering the world for practical application, in office they were renowned ministers. Literary composition and statecraft were brought together as one, not divided into two separate paths. Only when one possesses genuine learning in ordinary days can it be expressed as literary composition—like the brightness of the sun and moon, the resonance of metal and stone, the surging waves of rivers and seas, and the brilliant patterns of tigers and leopards—remedying defects and bolstering decline, so that the literary fortune of an entire era relies upon it for revival. translation_en: … those who select scholars and what the scholars expect of themselves will both be fulfilled without disappointment. Yet when scholars bow their heads over their books, surveying past and present and weighing the affairs of the world, they often passionately declare of themselves: "This responsibility belongs to none other than me!" When they finally step forth to take on grand and far-reaching charges, however, some seal their lips and say nothing, while others bind their hands and know not what to do. What then becomes of the ambitions they long cherished? Consider, too, how when the many scholars are recommended through the Provincial Examination, the Court throws open its gates and calls for men of talent to seek them out; we, Your Majesty's servants, seal the candidates' names, transcribe their papers, and exhaust our thoughts and concentrate our spirits to recognize them; and right away robes and caps are prepared for them, banquets with reed organs and zithers are held, and their family gates and lanes are honored with commemorative inscriptions to bestow special favor upon them. punctuated:
主庇民，以不負所學；使人謂有眞學問者有眞文章，竝有眞經濟；草野名儒，裕公輔重望；藏修碩彥，爲匡時偉人。此臣之所以勉多士，卽多士所以自勉，期於不愧科名，庶不負臣等今日之知，以上慰皇上側席之求，端於多士厚望焉；而臣心之滋懼者，乃得藉是稍釋也已。
兵部職方清吏司督捕主事臣徐銓謹序。
translation_en:
…the Sovereign and sheltering the people, so as not to fail what they have learned; causing people to say that those who possess genuine learning also possess genuine literary writing, and at the same time possess genuine statecraft; that renowned Confucian scholars from the countryside are richly endowed with the weighty prestige fit for high ministerial office; and that eminent worthies who have cultivated themselves in retirement become great men who rectify the age. This is wherewith your servant exhorts the many scholars, and it is likewise wherewith the many scholars should exhort themselves, hoping to be worthy of their examination honors, so as perhaps not to fail the recognition we have shown them today, and above to console the Emperor in his eager quest for talent—in truth placing deep hopes in the many scholars; and the growing trepidation in your servant's heart may by this means be slightly relieved.
Respectfully written as a preface by your servant Xu Quan 徐銓, Secretary for Fugitives in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War.
